  "note_markdown": "# Popularity-sensitive core decoding and a bounded-star-energy obstruction\n\n## Abstract\n\nFix a prime field $F_p$, dimension $m=2$, and an integer $100<d<p$. I prove an asymmetric refinement of the accepted-component decoder. If an accepted subgraph has point minimum degree $u$, line minimum degree $v$, line measure $\u03c4$, and $w=min(u,v)$, then the two conditions\n\n$$\nuv \\ge 2^{60}dp,\n\\qquad\nuw^2 \\ge 2^{60}d\u03c4p^2\n$$\n\nforce one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial to agree with the point table on at least $v/(800p)$ of all points.\n\nFor the original accepted graph, let $u_*$ be the largest point-degree threshold supporting accepted-incidence mass at least $\u03b5/2$. The component theorem implies\n\n$$\nu_*\u03b5^2 \\ge 2^{70}d\n\\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad\nagr(f,Q) \\ge \u03b5/12800.\n$$\n\nThus a hypothesis $u_*\\ge \u03ba \u03b5^a p$ gives the conditional threshold $\u03b5\\ge(2^{70}/\u03ba)^{1/(a+2)}(d/p)^{1/(a+2)}$. This interpolates from exponent $1/3$ at the universally available scale $u_*=\u03a9(\u03b5p)$ to exponent $1/2$ when $u_*=\u03a9(p)$. It does not improve the unconditional benchmark.\n\nI also prove a template-popularity lemma and a complementary obstruction: for every fixed star order, diffuse modal-constant tables can have star energy only $O(\u03b5^s)$ while every degree-101 global polynomial has agreement $o(\u03b5)$. Consequently, a scale-free bounded-order collision-energy increment cannot supply the missing popularity.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nThere are $p^2$ points and $p(p+1)$ affine lines. Every point lies on $p+1$ lines and every line contains $p$ points. Each affine line $L$ carries a univariate polynomial $P_L$ of degree at most the ambient integer $d$, and $f:F_p^2\\to F_p$ is the point table. The sampling rule is exactly a uniformly random affine line followed by a uniformly random point on it; equivalently, it is a uniform affine incidence. Put\n\n$$\n\u03b5=Pr_{L,\\,x\\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)].\n$$\n\nThe accepted graph has edge $(x,L)$ exactly when $x\\in L$ and $P_L(x)=f(x)$. All global polynomials below have total degree at most $d$.\n\nFor a subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$, let\n\n$$\nt=|T|,\n\\qquad\n\u03c4=\\frac{t}{p(p+1)},\n$$\n\nand let $u$ and $v$ denote its point-side and line-side minimum degrees, respectively. For the full accepted graph, write $a_x$ for the accepted degree of $x$ and define the absolute upper-tail incidence mass\n\n$$\n\u03b4_j=\\frac{1}{p^2(p+1)}\\sum_{x:a_x\\ge j}a_x,\n\\qquad\nu_*=max\\{j\\in\\{1,\\ldots,p+1\\}:\u03b4_j\\ge \u03b5/2\\}.\n$$\n\nWhen $\u03b5>0$, this set is nonempty. Since points below $\u03b5(p+1)/2$ carry less than half of all accepted edges,\n\n$$\nu_*\\ge \\left\\lceil\\frac{\u03b5(p+1)}2\\right\\rceil.\n$$\n\nFor $s\\ge2$, $\u0393_s$ denotes the probability that $s$ ordered distinct uniformly sampled lines through a uniform point all accept there.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe exact benchmark is Theorem 1.1 of [Kominers--Thaler--Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, Revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/): over every finite field, $\u03b5\\ge C(d/p)^{1/3}$ implies one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with agreement at least $c\u03b5$. The following explanation of the exponent is my reconstruction, not a separately quoted theorem: their Lemma 3.2 gives $|R|=O(p/\u03b5)$, Lemma 2.2 gives an explainer degree $D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\u03b5})$, and identity extension and lifting require $D=O(\u03b5p)$. Hence $\u03b5^3=\u03a9(d/p)$.\n\nThe present proof uses KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.1--2.3, 2.5--2.7, 6.1, and 6.3. The local cached KTZ file is the earlier July 2026 version; theorem numbering is stable, but the revision above is the pinned source. The cached Arora--Sudan file is the STOC 1997 version rather than the Combinatorica 2003 article recorded in the bibliography, and no theorem-number transfer from that cache is used.\n\nThe durable corpus was audited through [DATA_MANIFEST.json](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/DATA_MANIFEST.json), all eight active campaign-10 submissions, their verifier audits, all active leaderboards, and the empty campaign-300 leaderboards; directories named `superseded` were excluded. The main reusable prior result is the verifier-accepted symmetric component theorem in [researcher-0002](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0002/note.md). The exact pair-collision and regular-carrier obstruction in [researcher-0008](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0008/note.md) shows that graph regularity alone gives no energy surplus. The verified singular-lift obstruction in [researcher-0006](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0006/note.md) remains relevant to any future factorwise refinement.\n\nFor historical comparison only, Theorem 4.2 of [Harsha--Kumar--Saptharishi--Sudan, arXiv v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12752) states the bivariate condition $p>Cd/\u03b5^7$. It is not used in the proof.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A (proved asymmetric core decoder).** Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, and let $G=(X,T,E)$ be a nonempty accepted subgraph. Suppose every $x\\in X$ has degree at least the integer $u$, every $L\\in T$ has degree at least the integer $v$, $\u03c4=|T|/[p(p+1)]$, and $w=min(u,v)$. If\n\n$$\nuv\\ge2^{60}dp,\n\\qquad\nuw^2\\ge2^{60}d\u03c4p^2,\n$$\n\nthen there is a single $Q\\in F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying\n\n$$\nPr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\\ge\\frac{v}{800p}.\n$$\n\nConnectedness of the input is not required.\n\n**Corollary B (proved implication; conditional exponent).** With $u_*$ defined above, if\n\n$$\nu_*\u03b5^2\\ge2^{70}d,\n$$\n\nthen some total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial satisfies $agr(f,Q)\\ge \u03b5/12800$. More generally, if $0\\le a\\le1$, $0<\u03ba\\le1$, and $u_*\\ge \u03ba \u03b5^a p$, then the conclusion holds whenever\n\n$$\n\u03b5\\ge\\left(\\frac{2^{70}}\u03ba\\right)^{1/(a+2)}\n       \\left(\\frac dp\\right)^{1/(a+2)}.\n$$\n\nThe exponent improvement for $a<1$ is conditional because no such popularity tail is known for every table.\n\n**Lemma C (proved template popularity).** Let $T_1,\\ldots,T_R$ be disjoint line families and let $Q_1,\\ldots,Q_R$ be total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials such that $P_L=Q_j|_L$ for $L\\in T_j$. Let $\u03c4_j=|T_j|/[p(p+1)]$, $\u03c4=\\sum_j\u03c4_j$, let $\u03b4>0$ be the normalized accepted-incidence mass on their union, and put $\u03b1=max_j agr(f,Q_j)$. Then\n\n$$\n\u03b4\\le \u03b1\u03c4+\\sqrt{\\frac{R\u03b1\u03c4}{p+1}}.\n$$\n\nIn particular, $R\\le\u03b4(p+1)$ implies $\u03b1\\ge\u03b4/4$.\n\n**Proposition D (proved bounded-star-energy obstruction).** Fix $S\\ge2$. For all sufficiently large primes $p$, at the legal ambient degree $d=101$ there is a deterministic table using constant line polynomials such that, for\n\n$$\nr=\\left\\lfloor\\frac{\\log p}{4\\log\\log p}\\right\\rfloor,\n$$\n\none has\n\n$$\n\\frac{r}{130p}\\le \u03b5\\le\\frac{26r}{p},\n\\qquad\nmax_{deg Q\\le101}agr(f,Q)<\\frac2p,\n$$\n\nand, simultaneously for $2\\le s\\le S$,\n\n$$\n\u0393_s\\le2^{s+2}(S-1)\u03b5^s.\n$$\n\nA fully explicit sufficient meaning of sufficiently large is obtained by setting $u_0=\\lceil4\\log p/\\log\\log p\\rceil$ and $v_0=\\lceil8\\log p/\\log\\log p\\rceil$ and requiring\n\n$$\nr\\ge133,\n\\quad r^2\\le p,\n\\quad p\\ge8r!,\n\\quad u_0+1\\le17r,\n\\quad v_0\\le33r,\n$$\n\n$$\n\\frac{2p}{(u_0+1)!}\\le1,\n\\quad\n\\frac{2p^3}{v_0!}\\le\\frac18,\n\\quad\np^{5253}(e/4)^p\\le\\frac18,\n\\quad\nS\\le p+1.\n$$\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1] (proved: asymmetric mixing).** Put $\u03be=|X|/p^2$, $\u03c1=|E|/[p^2(p+1)]$, $\u03b1_0=u/(p+1)$, $\u03b2_0=v/p$, and $\u03bb=(p+1)^{-1/2}$. Minimum degree and KTZ Lemma 2.1 give\n\n$$\n\u03b1_0\u03be\\le\u03c1,\n\\qquad\n\u03b2_0\u03c4\\le\u03c1,\n\\qquad\n\u03c1\\le\u03be\u03c4+\u03bb\\sqrt{\u03be\u03c4}.\n$$\n\nIf $\u03c4<\u03b1_0/4$, the first and third inequalities imply $\u03be<(16/9)\u03bb^2\u03c4/\u03b1_0^2$. Substitution into the third inequality and comparison with $\u03b2_0\u03c4\\le\u03c1$ give $\u03b1_0\u03b2_0<2\u03bb^2$, or $uv<2p$. This contradicts the first hypothesis. The symmetric calculation gives\n\n$$\n\u03c4\\ge\\frac{u}{4(p+1)},\n\\qquad\n\u03be\\ge\\frac{v}{4p}.\n$$\n\nThus $t\\ge up/4$. Substituting the line-measure bound into the second hypothesis yields\n\n$$\nw^2\\ge\\frac{2^{60}dp^2}{4(p+1)}\\ge2^{57}dp.\n$$\n\nThis last inequality, rather than an unstated fixed-$d$ assumption, supplies all logarithmic room below.\n\n**[P2] (proved: selector and probability losses).** The first hypothesis and $v\\le p$ give $u>8$. Select every line of $T$ independently with probability $8/u$. A point accepted on a target line $L$ is called reached only through a selected line in $R$ other than $L$. It has at least $u-1$ eligible lines, so its reach probability exceeds $3/4$. For distinct points of $L$, the eligible line sets are disjoint because two distinct points determine their unique common line, which is the excluded line $L$. Chernoff therefore bounds the probability that at most half of $N_G(L)$ is reached by $e^{-v/24}$.\n\nSince $v\\ge w\\ge\\sqrt{2^{57}dp}$, $2p^2e^{-v/24}<1/4$; this accounts explicitly for the union bound over all target lines. The sample-size mean is $8t/u\\ge2p$. Its lower- and upper-tail Chernoff bounds are respectively at most $e^{-p/4}$ and $e^{-2p/3}$. Hence some choice has\n\n$$\n\\frac{4t}{u}\\le r=|R|\\le\\frac{16t}{u}\n$$\n\nand reaches more than half of every line's accepted points. In particular, $r\\ge p$.\n\n**[P3] (proved: interpolation).** Set\n\n$$\nD=16(\\lfloor\\sqrt{dr}\\rfloor+1).\n$$\n\nThen $D^2>256dr$ and\n\n$$\nD^2\\le1024dr\n \\le2^{14}\\frac{dt}{u}\n \\le2^{15}\\frac{d\u03c4p^2}{u}\n \\le2^{-45}w^2.\n$$\n\nThus $D<w/5000$, $D<p$, and $r\\ge p>D$. KTZ Lemma 2.2 gives $dim V_D\\ge D^3/(64d)>r(D+1)$. Each formal identity on a selected line costs at most $D+1$ homogeneous conditions, so a nonzero candidate in $V_D$ exists. If it were Z-independent, KTZ Lemma 2.5 and $r>D$ would force it to vanish identically. Its allowed positive Z-exponents are not divisible by $p$, so its Z-derivative is nonzero.\n\nLet $S_R$ be the finite union of the selected polynomial graphs and choose a nonzero polynomial $A$ of minimum weighted degree among polynomials vanishing on $S_R$ with $A_Z\\ne0$. KTZ Lemma 2.3 makes $A$ squarefree. Its weight is at most $D<p$, so pointwise vanishing at all $p$ parameters on a selected line is a formal identity. This also explains why repeated-factor removal cannot lose the line identities.\n\n**[P4] (proved: identity extension).** Every $L\\in T$ has more than $v/2>D$ accepted points reached through a selected $M\\ne L$. At such a point,\n\n$$\nP_L(x)=f(x)=P_M(x),\n$$\n\nso $A(x,P_L(x))=0$. The restricted polynomial $A(L(t),P_L(t))$ has degree at most $D$ and more than $D$ roots; hence it vanishes formally. There is no Markov or multiplicity loss at this step.\n\n**[P5] (proved: prime-field simple-root cleanup).** Write $A=HB$, where $H(X,Y)$ is the gcd of the Z-coefficients of $A$. At most $D$ affine lines are contained in $H=0$. On every other line, division in the integral domain $F_p[t]$ gives $B(L(t),P_L(t))\\equiv0$. The polynomial $B$ is squarefree, Z-primitive, Z-dependent, and has degree below $p$.\n\nMoreover, $gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. Indeed, if an irreducible $C$ divided both, squarefreeness and reduction of $(CE)_Z$ modulo $C$ would give $C|C_Z$, hence $C_Z=0$. Since $deg_Z C<p$, this makes $C$ Z-independent, contradicting Z-primitivity. KTZ Lemma 2.6 now bounds the lines on whose graphs both $B$ and $B_Z$ vanish by $D(D-1)$. On every other line, $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $D$, so it has at most $D$ accepted roots. Thus at most\n\n$$\npD^2+Dt\n$$\n\naccepted edges are deleted. No discriminant or derivative is divided by.\n\n**[P6] (proved: asymmetric pruning).** Since $|E|\\ge vt$,\n\n$$\n\\frac{pD^2+Dt}{|E|}\n \\le\\frac Dv+\\frac{pD^2}{vt}\n \\le\\frac Dv+\\frac{2^{14}dp}{uv}\n <\\frac1{4000}.\n$$\n\nLet $u_1=\\lfloor u/100\\rfloor$ and $v_1=\\lfloor v/100\\rfloor$. Iteratively delete point vertices of current degree below $u_1$ and line vertices below $v_1$. This costs less than\n\n$$\nu_1|X|+v_1|T|\\le |E|/50.\n$$\n\nA nonempty graph remains. The hypotheses imply $u_1\\ge u/200$, $v_1\\ge v/200$, and $u_1,v_1>D$.\n\n**[P7] (proved: lift, propagate, recover measure).** Every surviving point is incident to an identity line and hence satisfies $B(x,f(x))=0$; retained edges also certify $B_Z(x,f(x))\\ne0$. At a point in any surviving connected component, more than $D$ incident line roots satisfy the hypotheses of KTZ Lemma 6.1. It produces one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q$ with $B(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\\equiv0$. The one-variable simple-root uniqueness used in KTZ Lemma 6.3 propagates this same $Q$ through the component.\n\nSince $u_1v_1\\ge uv/40000>2p$, [P1]'s asymmetric mixing calculation applied to this component gives point density at least\n\n$$\n\\frac{v_1}{4p}\\ge\\frac{v}{800p}.\n$$\n\nThe polynomial agrees with $f$ at every point of that component, proving Theorem A. There is no list-size or factor-count loss.\n\n**[P8] (conditional: popularity-tail translation).** Let $\u03b4_*=\u03b4_{u_*}\\ge\u03b5/2$ and retain all accepted edges incident to points of degree at least $u_*$. Their number is $E_*=\u03b4_*p^2(p+1)$. Peel point degrees below $U=\\lfloor u_*/2\\rfloor$ and line degrees below $V=\\lfloor\u03b4_*p/4\\rfloor$. Point deletions cost at most $E_*/2$, and line deletions cost at most\n\n$$\nVp(p+1)\\le E_*/4.\n$$\n\nThus a nonempty core remains. Under $u_*\u03b5^2\\ge2^{70}d$, floors give\n\n$$\nU\\ge u_*/3,\n\\qquad\nV\\ge\u03b4_*p/8\\ge\u03b5p/16,\n\\qquad\nmin(U,V)\\ge\u03b5p/16.\n$$\n\nConsequently,\n\n$$\nUV\\ge u_*\u03b5p/48>2^{60}dp\n$$\n\nand, for every component line measure $\u03c4_C\\le1$,\n\n$$\nUmin(U,V)^2\n \\ge u_*\u03b5^2p^2/768\n >2^{60}d\u03c4_Cp^2.\n$$\n\nTheorem A gives agreement at least $V/(800p)\\ge\u03b5/12800$. If $u_*\\ge\u03ba \u03b5^a p$, the displayed hypothesis follows from $\u03ba \u03b5^{a+2}p\\ge2^{70}d$. Universally $u_*\\ge\u03b5p/2$, so this recovers exponent $1/3$ with a large constant. For $a<1$ it is a genuine conditional improvement; $a=0$ gives exponent $1/2$.\n\n**[P9] (proved: template popularity).** Put $S_j=\\{x:Q_j(x)=f(x)\\}$ and $\u03b1_j=|S_j|/p^2$. The carried edges in $T_j$ are exactly the incidences between $S_j$ and $T_j$. KTZ Lemma 2.1 gives\n\n$$\n\u03b4\\le\\sum_j\u03b1_j\u03c4_j+\n\\frac1{\\sqrt{p+1}}\\sum_j\\sqrt{\u03b1_j\u03c4_j}.\n$$\n\nThe first term is at most $\u03b1\u03c4$. Cauchy--Schwarz, the only loss here, bounds the second sum by $\\sqrt{R\u03b1\u03c4}$. This proves Lemma C. If $R\\le\u03b4(p+1)$ and $\u03b1<\u03b4/4$, the two right-hand terms are below $\u03b4/4$ and $\u03b4/2$, a contradiction.\n\n**[P10] (proved: constant-label branch).** For constant-labelled lines, group by their constant value $a$. The sets $\\{x:f(x)=a\\}$ are disjoint, so Cauchy--Schwarz uses $\\sum_aPr[f=a]=1$ and removes the $R$ factor:\n\n$$\n\u03b4\\le \u03bc\u03c4+\\sqrt{\\frac{\u03c4}{p+1}},\n\\qquad\n\u03bc=max_aPr[f=a].\n$$\n\nThus $\u03b4\\ge2\\sqrt{\u03c4/(p+1)}$ implies $\u03bc\\ge\u03b4/(2\u03c4)\\ge\u03b4/2$. If constant lines carry at least a $\u03b8$ fraction of the total agreement, then $\u03b5\\ge2/[\u03b8\\sqrt{p+1}]$ already yields a constant global polynomial of agreement at least $\u03b8\u03b5/2$.\n\n**[P11] (proved: exact star moments).** For every deterministic table,\n\n$$\n\u0393_s=\\frac{1}{p^2(p+1)_s}\\sum_x(a_x)_s.\n$$\n\nThe integer sequence $(n)_s$ is discretely convex. If $\u03bc=\u03b5(p+1)=k+\u03b8$ with integer $k=\\lfloor \u03bc\\rfloor$ and $0\\le\u03b8<1$, convexity gives the sharp degree-only lower bound\n\n$$\n\u0393_s\\ge\n\\frac{(1-\u03b8)(k)_s+\u03b8(k+1)_s}{(p+1)_s}.\n$$\n\nFor $s=2$, expansion yields the exact identity\n\n$$\n\u0393_2=\u03b5^2-\\frac{\u03b5(1-\u03b5)}p+\n\\frac{Var_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)}.\n$$\n\nThus even perfectly regular accepted degrees supply only baseline collision energy $\u0398(\u03b5^2)$.\n\n**[P12] (proved: modal occupancy and concentration).** Choose every value $f(x)$ independently and uniformly. The punctured incident lines partition all other points. Their values and the independent tie coins are independent. Label symmetry and double counting the $M$ modal positions show that each incident line accepts the point with probability exactly $q$. Hence $a_x$ is conditionally binomial and $E[\u0393_s]=q^s$.\n\nMarkov at threshold $4(S-1)q^s$, followed by a union bound over $2\\le s\\le S$, fails with probability at most $1/4$. On $\u03b5\\ge q/2$, this gives $\u0393_s\\le2^{s+2}(S-1)\u03b5^s$.\n\nFor each fixed total-degree-at-most-101 polynomial $Q$, its agreement count with random $f$ is $Bin(p^2,1/p)$, so\n\n$$\nPr[agr(f,Q)\\ge2/p]\\le(e/4)^p.\n$$\n\nThere are $p^{5253}$ candidates because $(101+1)(101+2)/2=5253$. NUMBERED NOTE:
0001: # Popularity-sensitive core decoding and a bounded-star-energy obstruction
0002: 
0003: ## Abstract
0004: 
0005: Fix a prime field $F_p$, dimension $m=2$, and an integer $100<d<p$. I prove an asymmetric refinement of the accepted-component decoder. If an accepted subgraph has point minimum degree $u$, line minimum degree $v$, line measure $τ$, and $w=min(u,v)$, then the two conditions
0006: 
0007: $$
0008: uv \ge 2^{60}dp,
0009: \qquad
0010: uw^2 \ge 2^{60}dτp^2
0011: $$
0012: 
0013: force one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial to agree with the point table on at least $v/(800p)$ of all points.
0014: 
0015: For the original accepted graph, let $u_*$ be the largest point-degree threshold supporting accepted-incidence mass at least $ε/2$. The component theorem implies
0016: 
0017: $$
0018: u_*ε^2 \ge 2^{70}d
0019: \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
0020: agr(f,Q) \ge ε/12800.
0021: $$
0022: 
0023: Thus a hypothesis $u_*\ge κ ε^a p$ gives the conditional threshold $ε\ge(2^{70}/κ)^{1/(a+2)}(d/p)^{1/(a+2)}$. This interpolates from exponent $1/3$ at the universally available scale $u_*=Ω(εp)$ to exponent $1/2$ when $u_*=Ω(p)$. It does not improve the unconditional benchmark.
0024: 
0025: I also prove a template-popularity lemma and a complementary obstruction: for every fixed star order, diffuse modal-constant tables can have star energy only $O(ε^s)$ while every degree-101 global polynomial has agreement $o(ε)$. Consequently, a scale-free bounded-order collision-energy increment cannot supply the missing popularity.
0026: 
0027: ## Test and Notation
0028: 
0029: There are $p^2$ points and $p(p+1)$ affine lines. Every point lies on $p+1$ lines and every line contains $p$ points. Each affine line $L$ carries a univariate polynomial $P_L$ of degree at most the ambient integer $d$, and $f:F_p^2\to F_p$ is the point table. The sampling rule is exactly a uniformly random affine line followed by a uniformly random point on it; equivalently, it is a uniform affine incidence. Put
0030: 
0031: $$
0032: ε=Pr_{L,\,x\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)].
0033: $$
0034: 
0035: The accepted graph has edge $(x,L)$ exactly when $x\in L$ and $P_L(x)=f(x)$. All global polynomials below have total degree at most $d$.
0036: 
0037: For a subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$, let
0038: 
0039: $$
0040: t=|T|,
0041: \qquad
0042: τ=\frac{t}{p(p+1)},
0043: $$
0044: 
0045: and let $u$ and $v$ denote its point-side and line-side minimum degrees, respectively. For the full accepted graph, write $a_x$ for the accepted degree of $x$ and define the absolute upper-tail incidence mass
0046: 
0047: $$
0048: δ_j=\frac{1}{p^2(p+1)}\sum_{x:a_x\ge j}a_x,
0049: \qquad
0050: u_*=max\{j\in\{1,\ldots,p+1\}:δ_j\ge ε/2\}.
0051: $$
0052: 
0053: When $ε>0$, this set is nonempty. Since points below $ε(p+1)/2$ carry less than half of all accepted edges,
0054: 
0055: $$
0056: u_*\ge \left\lceil\frac{ε(p+1)}2\right\rceil.
0057: $$
0058: 
0059: For $s\ge2$, $Γ_s$ denotes the probability that $s$ ordered distinct uniformly sampled lines through a uniform point all accept there.
0060: 
0061: ## Prior Results
0062: 
0063: The exact benchmark is Theorem 1.1 of [Kominers--Thaler--Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, Revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/): over every finite field, $ε\ge C(d/p)^{1/3}$ implies one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with agreement at least $cε$. The following explanation of the exponent is my reconstruction, not a separately quoted theorem: their Lemma 3.2 gives $|R|=O(p/ε)$, Lemma 2.2 gives an explainer degree $D=O(\sqrt{dp/ε})$, and identity extension and lifting require $D=O(εp)$. Hence $ε^3=Ω(d/p)$.
0064: 
0065: The present proof uses KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.1--2.3, 2.5--2.7, 6.1, and 6.3. The local cached KTZ file is the earlier July 2026 version; theorem numbering is stable, but the revision above is the pinned source. The cached Arora--Sudan file is the STOC 1997 version rather than the Combinatorica 2003 article recorded in the bibliography, and no theorem-number transfer from that cache is used.
0066: 
0067: The durable corpus was audited through [DATA_MANIFEST.json](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/DATA_MANIFEST.json), all eight active campaign-10 submissions, their verifier audits, all active leaderboards, and the empty campaign-300 leaderboards; directories named `superseded` were excluded. The main reusable prior result is the verifier-accepted symmetric component theorem in [researcher-0002](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0002/note.md). The exact pair-collision and regular-carrier obstruction in [researcher-0008](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0008/note.md) shows that graph regularity alone gives no energy surplus. The verified singular-lift obstruction in [researcher-0006](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0006/note.md) remains relevant to any future factorwise refinement.

0071: ## Theorem
0072: 
0073: **Theorem A (proved asymmetric core decoder).** Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, and let $G=(X,T,E)$ be a nonempty accepted subgraph. Suppose every $x\in X$ has degree at least the integer $u$, every $L\in T$ has degree at least the integer $v$, $τ=|T|/[p(p+1)]$, and $w=min(u,v)$. If
0074: 
0075: $$
0076: uv\ge2^{60}dp,
0077: \qquad
0078: uw^2\ge2^{60}dτp^2,
0079: $$
0080: 
0081: then there is a single $Q\in F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying
0082: 
0083: $$
0084: Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{v}{800p}.
0085: $$
0086: 
0087: Connectedness of the input is not required.
0088: 
0089: **Corollary B (proved implication; conditional exponent).** With $u_*$ defined above, if
0090: 
0091: $$
0092: u_*ε^2\ge2^{70}d,
0093: $$
0094: 
0095: then some total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial satisfies $agr(f,Q)\ge ε/12800$. More generally, if $0\le a\le1$, $0<κ\le1$, and $u_*\ge κ ε^a p$, then the conclusion holds whenever
0096: 
0097: $$
0098: ε\ge\left(\frac{2^{70}}κ\right)^{1/(a+2)}
0099:        \left(\frac dp\right)^{1/(a+2)}.
0100: $$
0101: 
0102: The exponent improvement for $a<1$ is conditional because no such popularity tail is known for every table.
0103: 
0104: **Lemma C (proved template popularity).** Let $T_1,\ldots,T_R$ be disjoint line families and let $Q_1,\ldots,Q_R$ be total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials such that $P_L=Q_j|_L$ for $L\in T_j$. Let $τ_j=|T_j|/[p(p+1)]$, $τ=\sum_jτ_j$, let $δ>0$ be the normalized accepted-incidence mass on their union, and put $α=max_j agr(f,Q_j)$. Then
0105: 
0106: $$
0107: δ\le ατ+\sqrt{\frac{Rατ}{p+1}}.
0108: $$
0109: 
0110: In particular, $R\leδ(p+1)$ implies $α\geδ/4$.
0111: 
0112: **Proposition D (proved bounded-star-energy obstruction).** Fix $S\ge2$. For all sufficiently large primes $p$, at the legal ambient degree $d=101$ there is a deterministic table using constant line polynomials such that, for
0113: 
0114: $$
0115: r=\left\lfloor\frac{\log p}{4\log\log p}\right\rfloor,
0116: $$
0117: 
0118: one has
0119: 
0120: $$
0121: \frac{r}{130p}\le ε\le\frac{26r}{p},
0122: \qquad
0123: max_{deg Q\le101}agr(f,Q)<\frac2p,
0124: $$
0125: 
0126: and, simultaneously for $2\le s\le S$,
0127: 
0128: $$
0129: Γ_s\le2^{s+2}(S-1)ε^s.
0130: $$
0131: 
0132: A fully explicit sufficient meaning of sufficiently large is obtained by setting $u_0=\lceil4\log p/\log\log p\rceil$ and $v_0=\lceil8\log p/\log\log p\rceil$ and requiring
0133: 
0134: $$
0135: r\ge133,
0136: \quad r^2\le p,
0137: \quad p\ge8r!,
0138: \quad u_0+1\le17r,
0139: \quad v_0\le33r,
0140: $$
0141: 
0142: $$
0143: \frac{2p}{(u_0+1)!}\le1,
0144: \quad
0145: \frac{2p^3}{v_0!}\le\frac18,
0146: \quad
0147: p^{5253}(e/4)^p\le\frac18,
0148: \quad
0149: S\le p+1.
0150: $$
0151: 
0152: ## Proof or Conditional Proof
0153: 
0154: **[P1] (proved: asymmetric mixing).** Put $ξ=|X|/p^2$, $ρ=|E|/[p^2(p+1)]$, $α_0=u/(p+1)$, $β_0=v/p$, and $λ=(p+1)^{-1/2}$. Minimum degree and KTZ Lemma 2.1 give
0155: 
0156: $$
0157: α_0ξ\leρ,
0158: \qquad
0159: β_0τ\leρ,
0160: \qquad
0161: ρ\leξτ+λ\sqrt{ξτ}.
0162: $$
0163: 
0164: If $τ<α_0/4$, the first and third inequalities imply $ξ<(16/9)λ^2τ/α_0^2$. Substitution into the third inequality and comparison with $β_0τ\leρ$ give $α_0β_0<2λ^2$, or $uv<2p$. This contradicts the first hypothesis. The symmetric calculation gives
0165: 
0166: $$
0167: τ\ge\frac{u}{4(p+1)},
0168: \qquad
0169: ξ\ge\frac{v}{4p}.
0170: $$
0171: 
0172: Thus $t\ge up/4$. Substituting the line-measure bound into the second hypothesis yields
0173: 
0174: $$
0175: w^2\ge\frac{2^{60}dp^2}{4(p+1)}\ge2^{57}dp.
0176: $$
0177: 
0178: This last inequality, rather than an unstated fixed-$d$ assumption, supplies all logarithmic room below.
0179: 
0180: **[P2] (proved: selector and probability losses).** The first hypothesis and $v\le p$ give $u>8$. Select every line of $T$ independently with probability $8/u$. A point accepted on a target line $L$ is called reached only through a selected line in $R$ other than $L$. It has at least $u-1$ eligible lines, so its reach probability exceeds $3/4$. For distinct points of $L$, the eligible line sets are disjoint because two distinct points determine their unique common line, which is the excluded line $L$. Chernoff therefore bounds the probability that at most half of $N_G(L)$ is reached by $e^{-v/24}$.
0181: 
0182: Since $v\ge w\ge\sqrt{2^{57}dp}$, $2p^2e^{-v/24}<1/4$; this accounts explicitly for the union bound over all target lines. The sample-size mean is $8t/u\ge2p$. Its lower- and upper-tail Chernoff bounds are respectively at most $e^{-p/4}$ and $e^{-2p/3}$. Hence some choice has
0183: 
0184: $$
0185: \frac{4t}{u}\le r=|R|\le\frac{16t}{u}
0186: $$
0187: 
0188: and reaches more than half of every line's accepted points. In particular, $r\ge p$.
0189: 
0190: **[P3] (proved: interpolation).** Set
0191: 
0192: $$
0193: D=16(\lfloor\sqrt{dr}\rfloor+1).
0194: $$
0195: 
0196: Then $D^2>256dr$ and
0197: 
0198: $$
0199: D^2\le1024dr
0200:  \le2^{14}\frac{dt}{u}
0201:  \le2^{15}\frac{dτp^2}{u}
0202:  \le2^{-45}w^2.
0203: $$
0204: 
0205: Thus $D<w/5000$, $D<p$, and $r\ge p>D$. KTZ Lemma 2.2 gives $dim V_D\ge D^3/(64d)>r(D+1)$. Each formal identity on a selected line costs at most $D+1$ homogeneous conditions, so a nonzero candidate in $V_D$ exists. If it were Z-independent, KTZ Lemma 2.5 and $r>D$ would force it to vanish identically. Its allowed positive Z-exponents are not divisible by $p$, so its Z-derivative is nonzero.
0206: 
0207: Let $S_R$ be the finite union of the selected polynomial graphs and choose a nonzero polynomial $A$ of minimum weighted degree among polynomials vanishing on $S_R$ with $A_Z\ne0$. KTZ Lemma 2.3 makes $A$ squarefree. Its weight is at most $D<p$, so pointwise vanishing at all $p$ parameters on a selected line is a formal identity. This also explains why repeated-factor removal cannot lose the line identities.
0208: 
0209: **[P4] (proved: identity extension).** Every $L\in T$ has more than $v/2>D$ accepted points reached through a selected $M\ne L$. At such a point,
0210: 
0211: $$
0212: P_L(x)=f(x)=P_M(x),
0213: $$
0214: 
0215: so $A(x,P_L(x))=0$. The restricted polynomial $A(L(t),P_L(t))$ has degree at most $D$ and more than $D$ roots; hence it vanishes formally. There is no Markov or multiplicity loss at this step.
0216: 
0217: **[P5] (proved: prime-field simple-root cleanup).** Write $A=HB$, where $H(X,Y)$ is the gcd of the Z-coefficients of $A$. At most $D$ affine lines are contained in $H=0$. On every other line, division in the integral domain $F_p[t]$ gives $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$. The polynomial $B$ is squarefree, Z-primitive, Z-dependent, and has degree below $p$.
0218: 
0219: Moreover, $gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. Indeed, if an irreducible $C$ divided both, squarefreeness and reduction of $(CE)_Z$ modulo $C$ would give $C|C_Z$, hence $C_Z=0$. Since $deg_Z C<p$, this makes $C$ Z-independent, contradicting Z-primitivity. KTZ Lemma 2.6 now bounds the lines on whose graphs both $B$ and $B_Z$ vanish by $D(D-1)$. On every other line, $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $D$, so it has at most $D$ accepted roots. Thus at most
0220: 
0221: $$
0222: pD^2+Dt
0223: $$
0224: 
0225: accepted edges are deleted. No discriminant or derivative is divided by.
0226: 
0227: **[P6] (proved: asymmetric pruning).** Since $|E|\ge vt$,
0228: 
0229: $$
0230: \frac{pD^2+Dt}{|E|}
0231:  \le\frac Dv+\frac{pD^2}{vt}
0232:  \le\frac Dv+\frac{2^{14}dp}{uv}
0233:  <\frac1{4000}.
0234: $$
0235: 
0236: Let $u_1=\lfloor u/100\rfloor$ and $v_1=\lfloor v/100\rfloor$. Iteratively delete point vertices of current degree below $u_1$ and line vertices below $v_1$. This costs less than
0237: 
0238: $$
0239: u_1|X|+v_1|T|\le |E|/50.
0240: $$
0241: 
0242: A nonempty graph remains. The hypotheses imply $u_1\ge u/200$, $v_1\ge v/200$, and $u_1,v_1>D$.
0243: 
0244: **[P7] (proved: lift, propagate, recover measure).** Every surviving point is incident to an identity line and hence satisfies $B(x,f(x))=0$; retained edges also certify $B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$. At a point in any surviving connected component, more than $D$ incident line roots satisfy the hypotheses of KTZ Lemma 6.1. It produces one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q$ with $B(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0$. The one-variable simple-root uniqueness used in KTZ Lemma 6.3 propagates this same $Q$ through the component.
0245: 
0246: Since $u_1v_1\ge uv/40000>2p$, [P1]'s asymmetric mixing calculation applied to this component gives point density at least
0247: 
0248: $$
0249: \frac{v_1}{4p}\ge\frac{v}{800p}.
0250: $$
0251: 
0252: The polynomial agrees with $f$ at every point of that component, proving Theorem A. There is no list-size or factor-count loss.
0253: 
0254: **[P8] (conditional: popularity-tail translation).** Let $δ_*=δ_{u_*}\geε/2$ and retain all accepted edges incident to points of degree at least $u_*$. Their number is $E_*=δ_*p^2(p+1)$. Peel point degrees below $U=\lfloor u_*/2\rfloor$ and line degrees below $V=\lfloorδ_*p/4\rfloor$. Point deletions cost at most $E_*/2$, and line deletions cost at most
0255: 
0256: $$
0257: Vp(p+1)\le E_*/4.
0258: $$
0259: 
0260: Thus a nonempty core remains. Under $u_*ε^2\ge2^{70}d$, floors give
0261: 
0262: $$
0263: U\ge u_*/3,
0264: \qquad
0265: V\geδ_*p/8\geεp/16,
0266: \qquad
0267: min(U,V)\geεp/16.
0268: $$
0269: 
0270: Consequently,
0271: 
0272: $$
0273: UV\ge u_*εp/48>2^{60}dp
0274: $$
0275: 
0276: and, for every component line measure $τ_C\le1$,
0277: 
0278: $$
0279: Umin(U,V)^2
0280:  \ge u_*ε^2p^2/768
0281:  >2^{60}dτ_Cp^2.
0282: $$
0283: 
0284: Theorem A gives agreement at least $V/(800p)\geε/12800$. If $u_*\geκ ε^a p$, the displayed hypothesis follows from $κ ε^{a+2}p\ge2^{70}d$. Universally $u_*\geεp/2$, so this recovers exponent $1/3$ with a large constant. For $a<1$ it is a genuine conditional improvement; $a=0$ gives exponent $1/2$.
0285: 
0286: **[P9] (proved: template popularity).** Put $S_j=\{x:Q_j(x)=f(x)\}$ and $α_j=|S_j|/p^2$. The carried edges in $T_j$ are exactly the incidences between $S_j$ and $T_j$. KTZ Lemma 2.1 gives
0287: 
0288: $$
0289: δ\le\sum_jα_jτ_j+
0290: \frac1{\sqrt{p+1}}\sum_j\sqrt{α_jτ_j}.
0291: $$
0292: 
0293: The first term is at most $ατ$. Cauchy--Schwarz, the only loss here, bounds the second sum by $\sqrt{Rατ}$. This proves Lemma C. If $R\leδ(p+1)$ and $α<δ/4$, the two right-hand terms are below $δ/4$ and $δ/2$, a contradiction.
0294: 
0295: **[P10] (proved: constant-label branch).** For constant-labelled lines, group by their constant value $a$. The sets $\{x:f(x)=a\}$ are disjoint, so Cauchy--Schwarz uses $\sum_aPr[f=a]=1$ and removes the $R$ factor:
0296: 
0297: $$
0298: δ\le μτ+\sqrt{\frac{τ}{p+1}},
0299: \qquad
0300: μ=max_aPr[f=a].
0301: $$
0302: 
0303: Thus $δ\ge2\sqrt{τ/(p+1)}$ implies $μ\geδ/(2τ)\geδ/2$. If constant lines carry at least a $θ$ fraction of the total agreement, then $ε\ge2/[θ\sqrt{p+1}]$ already yields a constant global polynomial of agreement at least $θε/2$.
0304: 
0305: **[P11] (proved: exact star moments).** For every deterministic table,
0306: 
0307: $$
0308: Γ_s=\frac{1}{p^2(p+1)_s}\sum_x(a_x)_s.
0309: $$
0310: 
0311: The integer sequence $(n)_s$ is discretely convex. If $μ=ε(p+1)=k+θ$ with integer $k=\lfloor μ\rfloor$ and $0\leθ<1$, convexity gives the sharp degree-only lower bound
0312: 
0313: $$
0314: Γ_s\ge
0315: \frac{(1-θ)(k)_s+θ(k+1)_s}{(p+1)_s}.
0316: $$
0317: 
0318: For $s=2$, expansion yields the exact identity
0319: 
0320: $$
0321: Γ_2=ε^2-\frac{ε(1-ε)}p+
0322: \frac{Var_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)}.
0323: $$
0324: 
0325: Thus even perfectly regular accepted degrees supply only baseline collision energy $Θ(ε^2)$.
0326: 
0327: **[P12] (proved: modal occupancy and concentration).** Choose every value $f(x)$ independently and uniformly. On each line choose uniformly among its modal values, using fresh independent line coins, and use that value as the constant polynomial $P_L$. Symmetric independent tie-breaking is essential; arbitrary deterministic tie-breaking need not give the claimed star identity.
0328: 
0329: Let $M$ be the maximum occupancy when $p$ balls are thrown into $p$ bins and let $q=E[M]/p=E[ε]$. If $Y$ counts bins of occupancy exactly $r$, the explicit conditions in Proposition D give
0330: 
0331: $$
0332: E[Y]\ge\frac{p}{8r!}\ge1,
0333: \qquad
0334: E[Y^2]\le E[Y]+\frac{p^2}{(r!)^2}\le65E[Y]^2.
0335: $$
0336: 
0337: The second-moment inequality gives $Pr[M\ge r]\ge1/65$, hence $q\ge r/(65p)$. Conversely, $Pr[M\ge s]\le p/s!$, so the stated factorial condition gives $E[M]\le u_0+1\le17r$.
0338: 
0339: Changing one point value changes maxima on only its $p+1$ incident lines and changes $ε$ by at most $1/p^2$. McDiarmid therefore gives
0340: 
0341: $$
0342: Pr[|ε-q|>q/2]
0343:  \le2exp(-q^2p^2/2)
0344:  \le2exp(-r^2/8450)
0345:  \le1/4.
0346: $$
0347: 
0348: **[P13] (proved: simultaneous low energy and no decoder).** Fix a point and condition on its value. The punctured incident lines partition all other points. Their values and the independent tie coins are independent. Label symmetry and double counting the $M$ modal positions show that each incident line accepts the point with probability exactly $q$. Hence $a_x$ is conditionally binomial and $E[Γ_s]=q^s$.
0349: 
0350: Markov at threshold $4(S-1)q^s$, followed by a union bound over $2\le s\le S$, fails with probability at most $1/4$. On $ε\ge q/2$, this gives $Γ_s\le2^{s+2}(S-1)ε^s$.
0351: 
0352: For each fixed total-degree-at-most-101 polynomial $Q$, its agreement count with random $f$ is $Bin(p^2,1/p)$, so
0353: 
0354: $$
0355: Pr[agr(f,Q)\ge2/p]\le(e/4)^p.
0356: $$
0357: 
0358: There are $p^{5253}$ candidates because $(101+1)(101+2)/2=5253$. Their union-bound failure is at most $1/8$. The probability that any line has modal occupancy at least $v_0$ is at most $2p^3/v_0!\le1/8$. All four bad-event probabilities total at most $3/4$, so a deterministic realization exists after freezing both $f$ and the tie coins. It has $r/(130p)\leε\le26r/p$, every line supports acceptance, every line accepts fewer than $v_0\le33r$ points, the stated star bounds, and no global decoder of agreement $2/p$.
0359: 
0360: **[P14] (refuted claim; obstruction proved).** Fix $s\ge2$, $γ>0$, and constants $c_0,c_1>0$. The scale-free assertion
0361: 
0362: $$
0363: max_{deg Q\le101}agr(f,Q)\le c_0ε
0364: \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
0365: Γ_s\ge c_1ε^{s-γ}
0366: $$
0367: 
0368: is false. Proposition D has global-to-local ratio below $260/r\to0$, while $Γ_s=O_s(ε^s)=o(ε^{s-γ})$. This does not refute a target-range energy lemma: for every fixed $η>0$,
0369: 
0370: $$
0371: \frac{ε}{(101/p)^{1-η}}
0372:  =O_η\left(\frac{r}{p^η}\right)\to0.
0373: $$
0374: 
0375: ## Exponent Ledger
0376: 
0377: | Stage | Input scale | Loss | Output scale | Status |
0378: |---|---|---|---|---|
0379: | KTZ reconstruction | $|R|=O(p/ε)$ | $D=O(\sqrt{dp/ε})$ and $D=O(εp)$ | $ε^3=Ω(d/p)$ | proved |
0380: | Asymmetric selector | $t=τp(p+1)$, point degree $u$ | Chernoff and one union bound; constants only | $r=Θ(τp^2/u)$ | proved |
0381: | Interpolation | $r$ line identities | $D=Θ(\sqrt{dr})$ | $D=O(\sqrt{dτp^2/u})$ | proved |
0382: | Identity/lift | roots $v$ and incident lines $u$ | require $D<min(u,v)$ | $u min(u,v)^2=Ω(dτp^2)$ | proved |
0383: | Cleanup | $pD^2+Dt$ bad edges | relative $D/v+O(dp/(uv))$ | $uv=Ω(dp)$ | proved |
0384: | Recovery | minima $u/100,v/100$ | affine mixing constant | agreement $Ω(v/p)$ | proved |
0385: | Popularity core | $u_*$ and mass $ε/2$ | $U=Ω(u_*),V=Ω(εp)$ | $u_*ε^2=Ω(d)$ | conditional |
0386: | Exponent translation | $u_*\geκ ε^a p$ | none beyond constants | $ε=Ω((d/p)^{1/(a+2)})$ | conditional |
0387: | Template branch | $R,δ,τ$ | $\sqrt{Rατ/p}$ by Cauchy--Schwarz | $R\leδp$ gives $α=Ω(δ)$ | proved |
0388: | Modal obstruction | $ε=Θ(r/p)$ | fixed-order Markov constants | $Γ_s=O_s(ε^s)$ and global $<2/p$ | proved |
0389: 
0390: Because $d/p<1$, the conditional exponent $1/(a+2)$ is stronger than $1/3$ exactly when $a<1$. Its largest value in this architecture is $1/2$, not the long-term $1-o(1)$ target.
0391: 
0392: ## Counterexample Attempts
0393: 
0394: The modal table is diffuse: every affine line in every direction supports acceptance, no line accepts more than $O(\log p/\log\log p)$ points, and yet every bounded star moment stays at its baseline scale. It rules out energy increments based only on a fixed number of coincident accepted lines.
0395: 
0396: The regular Hall carrier from the active corpus has full line support and pair energy $Θ(ε^2)$ but a perfect constant decoder. Together, the two examples show that low collision energy occurs in both easy and hard tables. An effective dichotomy must inspect algebraic coherence, not merely degrees or support.
0397: 
0398: Concentrating all good lines in $k$ directions gives $ε=k/(p+1)$ and $Γ_s=(k)_s/(p+1)_s$, but the planted global polynomial is immediate. Concentrated directions therefore do not refute the theorem.
0399: 
0400: Attempts based on $t^p-t$, Frobenius aliases, or inseparable line functions require degree at least $p$ and violate $d<p$. At the lower legal boundary, Proposition D uses ambient degree $d=101$; its constant line labels are allowed under that cap. For $d$ close to $p$, triangular interpolation gives every point table agreement at least $(d+1)(d+2)/(2p^2)$, exceeding $1/8$ once $d\ge(p-1)/2$. In particular, at $(p,d)=(103,101)$ it is $5253/10609\approx0.495$.
0401: 
0402: These are analytic falsification checks. No finite computation is used to prove an asymptotic soundness statement.
0403: 
0404: ## Characteristic Audit
0405: 
0406: All statements are restricted to the prime field. The proof enforces $D<p$ before any functional-to-formal conversion. The line labels have degree $d<p$, and the restricted explainer identities have degree at most $D<p$.
0407: 
0408: The interpolation space excludes positive Z-exponents divisible by the characteristic; in this prime-field parameter range, $D<p$ also prevents them directly. Minimum-weight interpolation is invoked only after a candidate with nonzero Z-derivative is constructed. Squarefreeness is therefore justified by the exact hypotheses of KTZ Lemma 2.3.
0409: 
0410: After Z-content removal, primitivity plus squarefreeness and $deg_ZB<p$ prove $gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. This directly handles irreducibility and inseparability; no generic derivative, discriminant division, or unverified separability assertion is needed. KTZ Lemma 2.6 applies its resultant only to this certified coprime pair. Newton lifting divides solely by a value of $B_Z$ retained as nonzero.
0411: 
0412: Ordinary multiplicity-one interpolation is used throughout. The selector's only union loss is $2p^2e^{-v/24}$, the modal star argument's Markov-plus-union loss is $1/4$, the global-polynomial union loss is $p^{5253}(e/4)^p$, and the only Cauchy--Schwarz loss in the template lemma is $\sqrt{Rατ/(p+1)}$.
0413: 
0414: ## Limitations
0415: 
0416: No unconditional popularity estimate stronger than $u_*=Ω(εp)$ is proved. Substituting that universal estimate into Corollary B recovers the cubic benchmark and nothing more, so `benchmark_improved=false`.
0417: 
0418: Even perfect point popularity $u_*=Θ(p)$ yields only exponent $1/2$ in this architecture because the simple-root cleanup and identity/lifting gates remain. Progress toward exponent $1-o(1)$ must replace those interfaces, not merely iterate the present popularity pruning.
0419: 
0420: The modal obstruction is scale-free and lies below every fixed target trigger. It does not rule out an energy increment whose hypothesis explicitly uses $ε\gtrsim(d/p)^{1-η}$, whose order grows with $p$, or whose energy records algebraic templates. Lemma C is useful only after such templates have actually been extracted; it does not produce them.
0421: 
0422: The constants are intentionally conservative and make Theorem A vacuous for modest fields. The result concerns only $m=2$, prime fields, total degree, and uniform affine-incidence sampling. No dimension lift, extension-field descent, or list-only conclusion is asserted.

This note isolates the algebraic obstruction left after introducing absolute factorization and discriminant curves into the affine line-versus-point test. A line table assigns to each line \\(L\\) one univariate polynomial \\(P_L\\) of degree at most \\(d\\), interpreted in any affine parameter on \\(L\\). For a point table \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\),\n\\[\n\\epsilon=\\Pr_{L,x\\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)]\n=\\frac{\\#\\{(L,x):x\\in L,\\ P_L(x)=f(x)\\}}{p^2(p+1)}.\n\\]\nLine sampling and then point sampling are both uniform. Arora\u2013Sudan Theorem 34 bounds bad affine specializations of an absolutely irreducible polynomial, while Lemma 35 and Corollary 36 use discriminants under a separability hypothesis; see the [journal paper](https://people.csail.mit.edu/madhu/papers/1997/arora-journ.pdf).\n\nFor plane curves, Aubry\u2013Perret Corollary 2.5 proves\n\\[\n|\\#C(\\mathbb F_p)-(p+1)|\\le(r-1)(r-2)\\sqrt p\n\\]\nfor an absolutely irreducible projective plane curve of degree \\(r\\); see the [primary paper](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~perret/Fichiers/Scan-Weil.Singulier.pdf). Cafure\u2013Matera Lemma 2.3 bounds rational points on an \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-irreducible but non-absolutely-irreducible curve; see the [primary text](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0405302v1). Neither point theorem controls how many graph directions pass through one lifted singular point.\n\nIn the active campaign corpus, researcher-0002 is the only accepted prior submission; its exponent-\\(1/2\\) consequence remains conditional on a small-component hypothesis. Researchers 0001 and 0004 require revision. Researcher-0003 was rejected because its headline theorem omitted essential interpolation hypotheses, although its verifier accepted the weighted-resultant calculation used below. To avoid inheriting the rejected statement, that calculation is proved again in [P2].\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem 1 (purification and singular-lift dichotomy).** Let \\(p\\) be prime and \\(101\\le d<p\\).\n\n1. **Frobenius purification.** Let \\(C\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]\\) be irreducible and \\(Z\\)-dependent, with weighted degree \\(\\delta\\), vertical degree \\(r\\), and \\(k\\ge2\\) absolute factors. If \\(\\mathcal T\\) is a family of distinct affine \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-lines with degree-at-most-\\(d\\) labels satisfying \\(C(L,P_L)\\equiv0\\), then\n   \\[\n   |\\mathcal T|\\le\\frac{2r\\delta-dr^2}{k^2}\n   \\le\\frac{\\delta^2}{dk^2}\n   \\le\\frac{\\delta^2}{4d}.\n   \\]\n   Consequently, for any primitive auxiliary polynomial of weight at most \\(D\\), all graph lines supported on geometrically reducible \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-factors number at most \\(D^2/(4d)\\).\n\n2. **Smooth ramification sparsity.** Fix one polynomial \\(B\\) and a graph-line family. If every ramified accepted lift \\(w=(x,f(x))\\) under consideration is smooth on \\(B=0\\), then their total number of accepted incidences is at most \\(p^2\\), giving normalized loss at most \\(1/(p+1)\\).\n\n3. **Linear regime.** If \\(d\\le D<2d\\) and \\(B\\) is primitive, \\(Z\\)-dependent, and of weight at most \\(D\\), then\n   \\[\n   B=a(X,Y)Z+b(X,Y),\\qquad\n   \\deg a\\le D-d,\n   \\quad \\deg b\\le D,\n   \\quad \\gcd(a,b)=1.\n   \\]\n   It is absolutely irreducible. Its ramified base set has at most \\(D(D-d)\\) points, no graph line is identically ramified, and deletion of all ramified base vertices costs at most \\(D(D-d)/p^2\\).\n\n4. **Sharp singular construction.** Suppose further that \\(d\\le p-2\\). Put \\(D=d+1\\), \\(s=\\lfloor(d+1)/2\\rfloor\\), and \\(e=d+1-2s\\). Choose distinct \\(c_1,\\ldots,c_s\\in\\mathbb F_p\\); if \\(e=1\\), choose \\(b\\notin\\{c_j\\}\\), and set\n   \\[\n   H(Y)=\\prod_{j=1}^s(Y-c_j)^2\\,(Y-b)^e,\n   \\qquad B(X,Y,Z)=XZ+H(Y).\n   \\]\n   Then \\(B\\) is a minimum-weight primitive, squarefree, absolutely irreducible graph interpolant of weight \\(D<p\\). There is a fully specified point/line table containing\n   \\[\n   sp>D\n   \\]\n   fully accepted lines, of line measure \\(s/(p+1)\\), with exactly one ramified accepted point per selected line. Their normalized ramified mass is \\(s/[p(p+1)]\\). The raw resultant is the smooth absolutely irreducible plane curve \\(X=0\\), but no total-degree-at-most-\\(d\\) polynomial restricts to all selected labels.\n\nNo part asserts a stronger soundness exponent or bounds the best global agreement for the explicit table.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n### [P1] Vertical separability \u2014 proved\n\nLet a squarefree polynomial \\(B\\), primitive in \\(Z\\), have weighted degree \\(\\delta<dp\\). Then \\(\\deg_ZB<p\\). If an irreducible factor \\(C\\) divided both \\(B\\) and \\(B_Z\\), squarefreeness would imply \\(C\\mid C_Z\\), so \\(C_Z=0\\). In characteristic \\(p\\), all its \\(Z\\)-exponents would then be multiples of \\(p\\). Since \\(\\deg_ZC<p\\), it would be independent of \\(Z\\), contradicting primitivity. Hence \\(\\gcd(B,B_Z)=1\\).\n\nThe strict threshold is necessary: \\(Z^p-X\\) has weighted degree \\(dp\\), is primitive, squarefree, smooth, and absolutely irreducible, but its \\(Z\\)-derivative is zero.\n\n### [P2] Weighted resultant line count \u2014 proved\n\nLet coprime \\(U,V\\) have weights \\(u,v\\) and vertical degrees \\(r_0,s_0\\). Their nonzero resultant \\(R=\\operatorname{Res}_Z(U,V)\\) has ordinary \\((X,Y)\\)-degree at most\n\\[\ns_0u+r_0v-dr_0s_0.\n\\]\nIndeed, every resultant monomial contains \\(s_0\\) coefficients of \\(U\\), \\(r_0\\) coefficients of \\(V\\), and total vertical-index weight \\(r_0s_0\\). Since the coefficient of \\(Z^i\\) in a weight-\\(u\\) polynomial has degree at most \\(u-di\\), the displayed bound follows term by term.\n\nIf both \\(U(L,P_L)\\) and \\(V(L,P_L)\\) vanish formally, then \\(R\\) vanishes identically on the base line \\(L\\). Its line equation divides \\(R\\). A nonzero bivariate polynomial of degree \\(E\\) has at most \\(E\\) distinct affine-line factors, proving the graph-line bound.\n\n### [P3] Frobenius purification \u2014 proved\n\nOver \\(\\overline{\\mathbb F}_p\\), Frobenius acts transitively on the \\(k\\) absolute factors of the \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-irreducible polynomial \\(C\\). Every factor has weight \\(\\delta/k\\) and vertical degree \\(r/k\\). If one factor vanishes on an \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-defined graph, applying Frobenius to that formal identity shows that every conjugate vanishes there. Two distinct conjugates are coprime, so [P2] gives\n\\[\n|\\mathcal T|\n\\le 2\\frac r k\\frac\\delta k-d\\left(\\frac r k\\right)^2\n=\\frac{2r\\delta-dr^2}{k^2}.\n\\]\nCompleting the square gives \\(2r\\delta-dr^2\\le\\delta^2/d\\), and \\(k\\ge2\\) gives the final \\(\\delta^2/(4d)\\) bound.\n\n### [P4] Union loss and sharpness \u2014 proved\n\nPrimitivity excludes base-only irreducible factors. Factor a primitive \\(B\\) over \\(\\mathbb F_p\\), assign each supported graph line to one factor, and apply [P3] to the geometrically reducible factors. If their weights are \\(\\delta_i\\), then\n\\[\n\\sum_i\\frac{\\delta_i^2}{4d}\n\\le\\frac{(\\sum_i\\delta_i)^2}{4d}\n\\le\\frac{D^2}{4d}.\n\\]\nThis is the sole union loss.\n\nThe constant is sharp. If \\(p>2d\\), choose a nonsquare \\(\\nu\\in\\mathbb F_p\\) and let \\(H_0\\) be the product of \\(d\\) distinct affine-line equations. Then\n\\[\nC=Z^2-\\nu H_0^2\n\\]\nis irreducible over \\(\\mathbb F_p\\), has \\(k=2\\), \\(r=2\\), and \\(\\delta=2d\\). It contains exactly the \\(d\\) base lines of \\(H_0\\) with label zero. If another graph existed, \\(q_L^2=\\nu H_0(L)^2\\) would make the nonsquare constant \\(\\nu\\) a square in \\(\\mathbb F_p(t)\\), which is impossible.\n\n### [P5] Smooth ramification sparsity \u2014 proved\n\nAt a ramified accepted lift \\(w=(x,f(x))\\), a formal graph identity along a line with direction \\(v_L\\) yields, by the chain rule,\n\\[\nB_X(w)v_{L,1}+B_Y(w)v_{L,2}+B_Z(w)P_L'(x)=0.\n\\]\nRamification removes the last term. Smoothness of \\(w\\) and \\(B_Z(w)=0\\) imply \\((B_X,B_Y)(w)\\ne(0,0)\\), whose kernel is one projective direction. Through \\(x\\) there is exactly one affine line of that direction. Thus each of the \\(p^2\\) base points supplies at most one such accepted edge. Division by a derivative is not used.\n\n### [P6] Linear-in-Z regime \u2014 proved\n\nIf \\(D<2d\\), positive vertical degree and the weight constraint force\n\\[\nB=aZ+b,\n\\quad \\deg a\\le D-d,\n\\quad \\deg b\\le D.\n\\]\nPrimitivity says \\(\\gcd(a,b)=1\\), and Gauss's lemma makes this primitive linear polynomial absolutely irreducible. A base point admits a ramified lift exactly when \\(a=b=0\\). B\u00e9zout therefore bounds the ramified base set by \\(\\deg(a)\\deg(b)\\le D(D-d)\\). Deleting a base point removes at most its \\(p+1\\) incidences, so its normalized cost is \\(1/p^2\\).\n\nIf a graph line were identically ramified, both \\(a\\) and \\(b\\) would vanish identically on its base line, contradicting their coprimality.\n\n### [P7] Algebra of the singular construction \u2014 proved\n\nThe polynomial \\(H\\) has degree \\(d+1\\), so \\(B=XZ+H(Y)\\) has weighted degree \\(D=d+1<p\\). As a polynomial in \\(Z\\), its coefficients \\(X,H(Y)\\) are coprime; hence it is primitive and absolutely irreducible by Gauss's lemma. It is consequently squarefree, and\n\\[\nB_Z=X,\n\\qquad \\gcd(B,B_Z)=1.\n\\]\nThe usual normalized discriminant of a degree-one polynomial is \\(1\\), whereas\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Res}_Z(B,B_Z)=X.\n\\]\nThus the raw resultant curve is a smooth absolutely irreducible line. At each lift \\((0,c_j,0)\\), however,\n\\[\nB_X=Z=0,\n\\quad B_Y=H'(c_j)=0,\n\\quad B_Z=X=0,\n\\]\nso the auxiliary hypersurface is singular there.\n\n### [P8] The full table and exact incidence counts \u2014 proved\n\nFor \\(j\\in\\{1,\\ldots,s\\}\\) and \\(m\\in\\mathbb F_p\\), take\n\\[\nL_{j,m}(t)=(t,c_j+mt),\n\\qquad\nP_{j,m}(t)=-\\frac{H(c_j+mt)}t.\n\\]\nThe quotient is a polynomial: for \\(m\\ne0\\), the double root at \\(c_j\\) makes the numerator divisible by \\(t^2\\); for \\(m=0\\), it is the zero polynomial. Its degree is at most \\(d\\), and\n\\[\nB(L_{j,m}(t),P_{j,m}(t))\\equiv0.\n\\]\nDefine\n\\[\nf(x,y)=\n\\begin{cases}\n-H(y)/x,&x\\ne0,\\\\\n0,&x=0,\n\\end{cases}\n\\]\nand set every unselected line label to zero. Every selected line is fully accepted, including its point \\(t=0\\). The \\(sp\\) lines are distinct, so they contribute agreement \\(s/(p+1)\\). Since \\(B_Z(L_{j,m}(t),P_{j,m}(t))=t\\), each has exactly one ramified accepted parameter. The normalized selected ramified mass is therefore\n\\[\n\\frac{sp}{p^2(p+1)}=\\frac{s}{p(p+1)}.\n\\]\nAt \\(p=103,d=101\\), \\(s=51\\), \\(D=102\\), and \\(sp=5{,}253\\).\n\n### [P9] Absence of a common global root and interpolation minimality \u2014 proved\n\nIf a total-degree-at-most-\\(d\\) polynomial \\(Q\\) restricted to every selected label, then\n\\[\nR(X,Y)=XQ(X,Y)+H(Y)\n\\]\nwould have total degree at most \\(D=d+1\\) and vanish identically on \\(sp>D\\) distinct affine lines. Their distinct line equations would all divide \\(R\\), forcing \\(R=0\\). This is impossible because \\(X\\nmid H(Y)\\).\n\nThere is also no nonzero graph interpolant of weighted degree at most \\(d\\). Such an interpolant must be \\(aZ+b(X,Y)\\) with constant \\(a\\). If \\(a=0\\), then \\(b\\) vanishes on more than \\(d\\) lines and is zero. If \\(a\\ne0\\), then \\(-b/a\\) is the forbidden polynomial \\(Q\\). Since \\(B\\) itself has weight \\(d+1\\), it is a minimum-weight interpolant.\n\n### [P10] Monic smooth-discriminant stress test \u2014 proved\n\nLet \\(2d\\le D<p\\), put \\(r=D-d\\), choose distinct \\(a_1,\\ldots,a_r\\in\\mathbb F_p\\), and set \\(A(X)=\\prod_i(X-a_i)\\). Then\n\\[\nB_{\\mathrm{sm}}=Z^2+A(X)Z+Y\n\\]\nis monic in \\(Z\\), has weight \\(D\\), and is smooth and absolutely irreducible because \\((B_{\\mathrm{sm}})_Y=1\\). Its discriminant\n\\[\n\\Delta=A(X)^2-4Y\n\\]\nis also smooth and absolutely irreducible. Nevertheless, on \\(L(t)=(t,0)\\) with the legal ambient-degree-\\(d\\) label \\(P_L=0\\),\n\\[\n(B_{\\mathrm{sm}})_Z(L(t),0)=A(t)\n\\]\nhas exactly \\(D-d\\) roots. Thus neither monicity nor smooth absolute irreducibility improves the pointwise per-line root bound. This agrees with [P5], because these roots occur at distinct base points and only one tangent direction is allowed at each.\n\n### [P11] Dense singular stress test \u2014 proved\n\nFor \\(p>4d+1\\), let \\(D=2d\\), choose distinct nonzero \\(a_1,\\ldots,a_{d-1}\\), put \\(g(X)=\\prod_i(X-a_i)\\), and define\n\\[\nB_{\\mathrm{den}}=Z^2-XYg(X)^2.\n\\]\nThe odd valuation of \\(Y\\) shows that \\(XYg^2\\) is not a square in \\(\\overline{\\mathbb F}_p(X,Y)\\); hence \\(B_{\\mathrm{den}}\\) is absolutely irreducible. For each nonzero square \\(s=c_s^2\\),\n\\[\nL_s(t)=(t,st),\n\\qquad P_s(t)=c_stg(t)\n\\]\nis a degree-\\(d\\) graph root. There are \\((p-1)/2>D\\) such lines, and \\((B_{\\mathrm{den}})_Z=2Z\\) has exactly the \\(d=D-d\\) roots \\(0,a_1,\\ldots,a_{d-1}\\) on every graph. A polynomial root would satisfy \\(Q^2=XYg^2\\), contradicting the odd \\(Y\\)-valuation. All these ramified lifts are singular, so [P5] is not contradicted.\n\n### [P12] Tempting replacements for simplicity \u2014 refuted\n\nThe following claims are false:\n\n- absolute irreducibility plus more than \\(D\\) graph lines forces a global polynomial root without a simple common lift;\n- a smooth absolutely irreducible raw-resultant curve controls graph-direction multiplicity;\n- smooth absolute irreducibility of a monic discriminant gives \\(o(D-d)\\) ramified parameters on every graph line.\n\nThey are refuted respectively by [P7]\u2013[P9], [P7]\u2013[P8], and [P10]. The correct positive statement is [P5]: smoothness must hold at the lifted point on \\(B=0\\), not merely generically or on the projected resultant curve.\n\n### [P13] Exponent consequence \u2014 conditional\n\nUnder the KTZ upper envelope \\(D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\), [P3] purges geometrically reducible factors at normalized cost \\(O(1/(\\epsilon p))\\), and [P5] would charge smooth ramification by \\(1/(p+1)\\). These are improvements over a blanket \\(D/p\\) charge, but only after assigning incidences to a fixed factor and proving the required smoothness.\n\nThe explicit constructions show that absolute irreducibility does not supply that smoothness. If singular incidences are still charged by \\(D/p\\), the comparison\n\\[\n\\sqrt{\\frac d{\\epsilon p}}=O(\\epsilon)\n\\]\nagain yields \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\). This is an architecture diagnosis, not a proof that every possible method must remain cubic.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input scale | Exact loss | Output or requirement | Status |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---|\n| KTZ benchmark | \\(\\epsilon\\ge C(d/p)^{1/3}\\) | Published proof losses | global agreement \\(c\\epsilon\\) | quoted/proved |\n| KTZ reconstruction | \\(|\\mathcal R|\\le6400p/\\epsilon\\) | \\(D/p\\le1280\\sqrt{d/(\\epsilon p)}+16/p\\) | \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\) suffices | proved reconstruction |\n| Frobenius purification | factor weights \\(\\delta_i\\) | \\(\\sum_i\\delta_i^2/[4dp(p+1)]\\le D^2/[4dp(p+1)]\\) | only absolute factors remain | proved |\n| Purification at KTZ envelope | \\(D^2=O(dp/\\epsilon)\\) | \\(O(1/(\\epsilon p))\\) | needs \\(\\epsilon^2p=\\Omega(1)\\) to be \\(O(\\epsilon)\\) | conditional |\n| Smooth fixed factor | at most \\(p^2\\) edges | \\(1/(p+1)\\) | needs \\(\\epsilon p=\\Omega(1)\\) | proved |\n| Linear regime | \\(d\\le D<2d\\) | \\(D(D-d)/p^2\\) | vertex-based cleanup | proved |\n| Singular table | \\(D=d+1\\), \\(s=\\lfloor(D/2)\\rfloor\\) | \\(s/[p(p+1)]\\) | \\(\\epsilon_{\\rm tab}\\ge s/(p+1)\\); no global-agreement claim | proved |\n| Residual per-line method | \\(D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\) | \\(D/p=O(\\sqrt{d/(\\epsilon p)})\\) | cubic threshold remains | conditional |\n\nThe new arguments use one explicit union bound in [P4]. They use no Markov inequality, Cauchy\u2013Schwarz inequality, point-line mixing, interpolation multiplicity, or division by a derivative.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Degree-drop discriminant attack:** successful against normalized discriminants. For \\(B=XZ+H(Y)\\), \\(\\operatorname{Disc}_ZB=1\\) but the raw resultant is \\(X\\); the omitted fiber contains every singular accepted lift.\n2. **Absolute plane-curve attack:** unsuccessful as a route to soundness. The raw-resultant curve \\(X=0\\) is already smooth, absolutely irreducible, and has the expected \\(p\\) rational points. The missing statistic is directional multiplicity above its points.\n3. **Monic repair:** unsuccessful. The construction in [P10] removes leading-coefficient degeneration and keeps both the hypersurface and discriminant smooth, but still attains \\(D-d\\) roots on one line.\n4. **Many-direction repair:** unsuccessful. The constructions in [P8] and [P11] have more than \\(D\\) graph lines and no global polynomial root; the common lifted points are singular.\n5. **Endpoint \\(d=p-1\\):** the attempted singular construction fails under \\(D<p\\). Here \\(D=d\\), and every primitive \\(Z\\)-dependent interpolant directly yields \\(Z-Q\\).\n6. **Adversarial full tables:** [P8] is a full table with uniform sampling and explicit agreement. It is not a soundness counterexample: for example, its point table has substantial structured zero sets, so some global polynomial can have nontrivial agreement even though none matches every selected label.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- Because \\(d>100\\) and \\(d<p\\), the prime \\(p\\) is odd. The uses of \\(2^{-1}\\) and nonsquares are safe.\n- [P1] identifies the actual inseparability threshold \\(\\operatorname{wdeg}B<dp\\). The commonly imposed \\(D<p\\) is stronger and is needed for other polynomial-identity/root-count steps, not for vertical separability itself.\n- Frobenius in [P3] is used only to compare absolute factors of an \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-polynomial. The test remains over the prime field; there is no extension-field test or descent.\n- The quotient in [P8] is exact polynomial division. No value \\(t=0\\) is inverted.\n- The standard discriminant/resultant distinction is explicit. For degree one, normalizing by the leading coefficient loses degree-dropping fibers.\n- The lower boundary is tested at \\(p=103,d=101,D=102\\). No case with \\(d\\le100\\) is invoked.\n- The construction covers \\(d=p-2\\). At \\(d=p-1\\), the separate linear argument yields a graph polynomial immediately.\n- Local labels have degree at most the ambient \\(d\\); global degree is total degree. No individual-degree substitution is made.\n- The selected lines in [P8] use all \\(p\\) nonvertical directions, with \\(s\\) translates in each direction. The obstruction is therefore not caused by concentration in a small direction set.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThis note does not prove a bivariate soundness theorem beyond KTZ, does not claim a new exponent, and does not bound the best global agreement for its explicit tables. It shows only that an absolute-factor/discriminant strategy must separately control singular accepted lifts.\n\nThe purification loss \\(O(1/(\\epsilon p))\\) requires \\(\\epsilon^2p=\\Omega(1)\\) if discarded outright. That condition is harmless under the cubic benchmark but can fail in parts of the intended \\((d/p)^{1-o(1)}\\) regime. A more refined component argument is still needed.\n\nAlthough [P9] proves that \\(B=XZ+H(Y)\\) is a minimum-weight interpolant for its displayed graph constraints, this note does not prove that the exact randomized reference-set and component-selection stages of KTZ necessarily output that factor. Conversely, it does not prove that those stages eliminate it.\n\nFinally, Weil-type plane-curve estimates count rational points, whereas this bottleneck concerns accepted graph directions and multiplicities above those points.
