research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0007/response.json:162:  "note_markdown": "# Factorwise Weighted-Polar Accounting and a Sharp Whole-Relation Obstruction\n\n## Abstract\n\nFix dimension two over the prime field $F_p$, with $101\u2264d<p$. I prove a factorwise weighted-resultant lemma for the polynomial graph curves appearing after bivariate interpolation. Once a primitive squarefree relation $B$ is factored, every graph line may be assigned to an irreducible factor that vanishes on it. For the assigned factor $C_i$, both identically ramified lines and finite ramification points are controlled by its own weighted degree and its own vertical polar $C_{i,Z}$, rather than by the degree of all of $B$. A cleaned connected factor class of minimum degree $k$ yields one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with global agreement at least $k/(4p)$.\n\nThe adversarial half is sharp. For every $2d\u2264D<p$, an explicit primitive squarefree relation and a legal line-versus-point table attain exactly $D-d$ simple whole-relation polar intersections on every supported line. When $p\u22658d$ the parameters may be chosen so that $\u03b5=\u0398((d/p)^{1/3})$ and $D=\u0398(sqrt(dp/\u03b5))=\u0398(\u03b5p)$. Thus raw B\u00e9zout or intersection-multiplicity accounting cannot improve the whole-$B$ ramification term. All bad roots in the example are cross-factor collisions; assigning the graphs to the factor $Z$ removes them completely. This identifies factor consistency, not a sharper unfactored root count, as the missing step. The unconditional benchmark is not improved.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nFix a prime $p$ and an integer $101\u2264d<p$; throughout $m=2$. There are $p(p+1)$ affine lines in $F_p\u00b2$, each with $p$ points. The test chooses an affine line uniformly and then a point uniformly on it. Its incidence denominator is $p\u00b2(p+1)$.\n\nLet $f:F_p\u00b2\u2192F_p$, and let every line $L$ carry $P_L\u2208F_p[t]$ of degree at most $d$. Put\n\n$$\n\u03b5=Pr_{L,x\u2208L}[P_L(x)=f(x)].\n$$\n\nGlobal candidates always have total degree at most $d$. Give $X,Y,Z$ weights $1,1,d$. For a polynomial $F$, write $wdeg(F)$ for this weighted degree. If $\u03b3_L(t)=(L(t),P_L(t))$, then\n\n$$\ndeg_t F(\u03b3_L(t))\u2264wdeg(F).\n$$\n\nIf $F(\u03b3_L)$ is nonzero and vanishes at $t_0$, define its local graph intersection multiplicity to be $ord_{t_0}F(\u03b3_L(t))$. This is the intersection multiplicity of the parametrized graph with the divisor $F=0$ on the normalization of the graph curve.\n\nA polynomial in $F_p[X,Y,Z]$ is primitive in $Z$ when the gcd in $F_p[X,Y]$ of its $Z$-coefficients is one.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe active corpus contains four submissions and four audits. Researcher 0002 is verified; its component-sensitive decoder gives a conditional exponent $1/2$. Researchers 0001 and 0004 require revision; they respectively isolate support-sensitive cubic closure and a rank-blind multiplicity barrier. Researcher 0003 was rejected because its exact theorem string omitted the hypotheses forcing a genuinely $Z$-dependent primitive interpolant, although the weighted-resultant calculation in its detailed proof was judged sound under the fuller hypotheses. The campaign-300 leaderboards are empty. The data manifest is a stale pre-launch snapshot relative to the populated campaign-10 boards, so the live files were used. Every directory named `superseded` was excluded.\n\nThe quoted benchmark is [Kominers\u2013Thaler\u2013Zheng, Revision 1, Theorem 1.1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download). Its specialization to $q=p,m=2$ says that\n\n$$\n\u03b5\u2265C(d/p)^{1/3}\n$$\n\nimplies one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with agreement at least $c\u03b5$. The theorem statement leaves $c$ unspecified; Lemmas 6.2\u20136.3 in the bivariate proof give $\u03b5/8000$.\n\nKTZ Lemma 2.6 is the exact source result closest to B\u00e9zout: for coprime trivariate polynomials of ordinary total degrees $u,v$, at most $uv$ polynomial graph lines can be common zeros. It eliminates $Z$ with a resultant and invokes Lemma 2.5 on the resulting bivariate polynomial. KTZ Lemma 5.1 obtains $D(D-1)$ exceptional lines from this ordinary-degree estimate. The weighted formula and the factor assignment below are proved here; neither is quoted from KTZ.\n\nThe cubic calculation is also a reconstruction, not a quoted theorem. KTZ Lemma 3.2 gives $|R|=O(p/\u03b5)$; Lemmas 2.2 and 4.1\u20134.2 give $D=O(sqrt(dp/\u03b5))$; Lemmas 4.3, 5.2, and 6.1 require $D=O(\u03b5p)$. Therefore $\u03b5\u00b3=\u03a9(d/p)$. The resultant-line deletion alone is weaker. [HKSS Lemmas 2.10 and 3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.12752v1) are used only as a source cross-check for simple-root Newton uniqueness.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A \u2014 factorwise weighted-polar accounting.** Let $p$ be prime and $101\u2264d<p$. Let $B\u2208F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be primitive in $Z$, squarefree, of positive $Z$-degree, and of weighted degree $\u03b4<p$. Write\n\n$$\nB=c\u220f_{i=1}^s C_i\n$$\n\nas a product of distinct irreducibles over $F_p$. Put\n\n$$\n\u03b4_i=wdeg(C_i),\\quad r_i=deg_Z(C_i),\\quad \u03b3_i=wdeg(C_{i,Z}),\n$$\n\nand\n\n$$\n\u039e_i=(r_i-1)\u03b4_i+r_i\u03b3_i-dr_i(r_i-1).\n$$\n\nLet $T$ be a family of distinct affine lines with degree-at-most-$d$ labels, and let $T=\u2294_iT_i$ be a chosen partition such that\n\n$$\nC_i(L(t),P_L(t))\u22610\\qquad(L\u2208T_i).\n$$\n\nLet $e_i$ be the number of $L\u2208T_i$ for which $C_{i,Z}(L(t),P_L(t))\u22610$. Then\n\n$$\ne_i\u2264min\\{|T_i|,\u039e_i\\}.\n$$\n\nOn every other line in $T_i$,\n\n$$\nsum_{t\u2208F_p}ord_t C_{i,Z}(L(t),P_L(t))\u2264\u03b3_i.\n$$\n\nFor every point table $f$, the number of accepted incidences satisfying $C_{i(L),Z}(x,f(x))=0$ is at most\n\n$$\nsum_i\\bigl(pe_i+(|T_i|-e_i)\u03b3_i\\bigr).\n$$\n\nConsequently, its uniform-incidence measure is at most\n\n$$\nfrac{sum_i min\\{|T_i|,\u039e_i\\}}{p(p+1)}\n+\nfrac{sum_i|T_i|\u03b3_i}{p\u00b2(p+1)}.\n$$\n\nMoreover, $\u03b3_i\u2264\u03b4_i-d$ and\n\n$$\n\u039e_i\u2264(2r_i-1)\u03b4_i-dr_i\u00b2\u2264\u03b4_i\u00b2/d-\u03b4_i.\n$$\n\nWriting $\u03c4_i=|T_i|/[p(p+1)]$, $\u03c4=sum_i\u03c4_i$, and $bar\u03b4=(sum_i\u03c4_i\u03b4_i)/\u03c4$ for $\u03c4>0$, the coarser bound is\n\n$$\nfrac{\u03b4\u00b2/d-\u03b4}{p(p+1)}+frac{\u03c4(bar\u03b4-d)}p.\n$$\n\n**Corollary B \u2014 cleaned factor component.** Under Theorem A, fix $i$. Let $G=(X,T',E')$ be a connected subgraph of accepted incidences with $T'\u2286T_i$, minimum degree at least the integer $k$, and $C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))\u22600$ on every edge. If\n\n$$\nk>\u03b4_i,\\qquad frac1{sqrt(p+1)}\u2264frac{k}{4p},\n$$\n\nthen there is $Q\u2208F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that\n\n$$\nQ(x)=f(x)\\quad(x\u2208X),\\qquad Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\u2265frac{k}{4p}.\n$$\n\n**Theorem C \u2014 sharpness of the whole-relation polar term.** Let $p$ be prime and let the integers satisfy\n\n$$\n101\u2264d,\\qquad 2d\u2264D<p.\n$$\n\nThere exist a primitive squarefree $B$ of weighted degree $D$, a point table, and degree-at-most-$d$ line labels such that the test agreement is\n\n$$\n\u03b5=frac{D-d}{p+1},\n$$\n\nall accepted incidences lie on nonvertical graph lines satisfying $B(L(t),P_L(t))\u22610$, and every accepted incidence is a simple zero of $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$. If $\u03c4=p/(p+1)$ is the measure of the nonvertical lines, then the ramified-incidence measure is exactly\n\n$$\n\u03b5=frac{\u03c4(D-d)}p.\n$$\n\nThe same graph lines admit an assignment to a factor $C$ with $C_Z=1$, and a total-degree-zero polynomial has global agreement $(D-d)/p>\u03b5$.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1] (proved: factor separability).** If an irreducible factor $C_i$ were independent of $Z$, it would divide every $Z$-coefficient of $B$, contradicting primitivity. Thus $r_i\u22651$. Since $r_i\u2264\u03b4_i/d\u2264\u03b4/d<p$, differentiation does not kill its leading $Z$-term. Hence $C_{i,Z}\u22600$. Irreducibility and the smaller $Z$-degree give $gcd(C_i,C_{i,Z})=1$. No absolute irreducibility is used.\n\n**[P2] (proved: weighted resultant degree).** Write\n\n$$\nU=sum_{a=0}^r u_a(X,Y)Z^a,\\qquad V=sum_{b=0}^s v_b(X,Y)Z^b\n$$\n\nwith weighted degrees $u,v$. Then $deg(u_a)\u2264u-da$ and $deg(v_b)\u2264v-db$. Every monomial of the Sylvester determinant contains $s$ coefficients of $U$, $r$ coefficients of $V$, and has aggregate coefficient-index sum $rs$. Therefore\n\n$$\ndeg_{X,Y}Res_Z(U,V)\u2264su+rv-drs.\n$$\n\nThis proof uses the determinant directly and performs no division by a leading coefficient. If one $Z$-degree is zero, the same formula is the direct degree bound for that base polynomial.\n\n**[P3] (proved: exceptional graph lines with multiplicity).** Apply [P2] to $U=C_i$ and $V=C_{i,Z}$. Their $Z$-degrees are $r_i,r_i-1$, and their weighted degrees are $\u03b4_i,\u03b3_i$. By [P1], the resultant $R_i=Res_Z(C_i,C_{i,Z})$ is nonzero and\n\n$$\ndeg R_i\u2264\u039e_i.\n$$\n\nIf both restrictions vanish identically on a graph over $L$, specialization of the Sylvester determinant vanishes identically on the base line. Its affine-linear equation divides $R_i$. More precisely, with $\u03bd_L=ord_{ell_L}(R_i)$,\n\n$$\nsum_{L\u2208T_i:C_{i,Z}|_L\u22610}\u03bd_L\u2264deg R_i\u2264\u039e_i.\n$$\n\nSince every $\u03bd_L\u22651$, this proves the exceptional-line count.\n\n**[P4] (proved: finite polar intersections).** On a nonexceptional line, the pullback\n\n$$\ng_L(t)=C_{i,Z}(L(t),P_L(t))\n$$\n\nis a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $\u03b3_i$. Its roots, counted with their orders, therefore sum to at most $\u03b3_i$. Accepted ramified incidences are a subset of these roots. This is the complete local intersection-multiplicity charge; no multiplicity is suppressed.\n\n**[P5] (proved: normalized factorwise loss).** An exceptional line contributes at most $p$ accepted incidences, and every other assigned line contributes at most $\u03b3_i$. Summing [P3]\u2013[P4] and dividing by $p\u00b2(p+1)$ gives Theorem A's exact and relaxed bounds. Differentiation lowers weighted degree by at least $d$, so $\u03b3_i\u2264\u03b4_i-d$. Substitution in $\u039e_i$ yields\n\n$$\n\u039e_i\u2264(2r_i-1)\u03b4_i-dr_i\u00b2\n=\u03b4_i\u00b2/d-\u03b4_i-(\u03b4_i-dr_i)\u00b2/d.\n$$\n\nFinally, weighted degree is additive under products, so $sum_i\u03b4_i=\u03b4$, and $sum_i\u03b4_i\u00b2\u2264\u03b4\u00b2$. This proves the coarse expression.\n\n**[P6] (conditional: one factor class decodes).** At any point of $G$, an incident graph identity and acceptance give $C_i(x,f(x))=0$; the cleaned-edge hypothesis makes this root simple. Choose a point $b$. It has at least $k>\u03b4_i$ incident lines. The simple-root Newton recursion, exactly KTZ Lemmas 2.7 and 6.1 with degree $\u03b4_i$, constructs $Q$ of total degree at most $d$, agrees with every incident line label, and satisfies $C_i(X,Y,Q)\u22610$. It divides only by $C_{i,Z}(b,f(b))$.\n\nSimple-root uniqueness propagates the same $Q$ throughout the connected component. For completeness, let $a,b_0,\u03c1$ be its normalized point, line, and edge measures, put $\u03ba=k/p$ and $u=1/sqrt(p+1)$. Minimum degree and affine incidence mixing give\n\n$$\n\u03c1\u2265\u03baa/2,\\qquad \u03c1\u2265\u03bab_0,\\qquad \u03c1\u2264ab_0+u sqrt(ab_0).\n$$\n\nIf $a<\u03ba/4$, the second and third inequalities imply $b_0<a/9$; substituting this into the upper bound contradicts $\u03c1\u2265\u03baa/2$. If $b_0<\u03ba/4$, the first and third imply $a<b_0$; substitution contradicts $\u03c1\u2265\u03bab_0$. Thus $a,b_0\u2265\u03ba/4$, proving global agreement at least $k/(4p)$. This is the only Cauchy\u2013Schwarz loss in the new decoder.\n\n**[P7] (proved: construction).** Put $e=D-d$. Choose $S\u2282F_p$ with $|S|=e$ and set\n\n$$\nH(X)=prod_{a\u2208S}(X-a),\\qquad B=Z(Z-H(X)).\n$$\n\nBecause $e\u2265d$, $wdeg(B)=max\\{2d,d+e\\}=D$. The two distinct factors $Z$ and $Z-H$ make $B$ squarefree, and its leading $Z\u00b2$ coefficient one makes it primitive.\n\nSet $f(x,y)=0$ for $x\u2208S$ and $f(x,y)=1$ otherwise. Give every nonvertical line the constant label zero and every vertical line the constant label two. Since $p>d\u2265101$, the value two differs from zero and one. Vertical lines have no accepted points. A nonvertical parameterization has $X=u+vt$ with $v\u22600$, so it contains exactly $e$ accepted points.\n\nThere are $p\u00b2$ nonvertical lines. Hence the accepted-incidence count is $ep\u00b2$, and\n\n$$\n\u03b5=frac{ep\u00b2}{p\u00b2(p+1)}=frac e{p+1}.\n$$\n\n**[P8] (proved: exact intersection saturation).** On every nonvertical zero-labelled graph,\n\n$$\nB(L(t),0)\u22610,\\qquad B_Z(L(t),0)=-H(u+vt).\n$$\n\nThe latter has exactly $e=D-d$ roots. They are simple because $H$ has distinct roots and $v\u22600$, and they are exactly the accepted parameters. Thus every accepted incidence is removed by whole-$B$ vertical cleanup and its normalized mass is\n\n$$\nfrac e{p+1}=frac{p}{p+1}frac{D-d}{p}.\n$$\n\nAt every such lifted point, $B_X=B_Y=B_Z=0$. There are $ep$ lifted singular points, each incident to $p$ accepted nonvertical graph lines, giving $ep\u00b2$ ramified incidences. Counting base points instead of incidences therefore does not save a factor. Nevertheless every relevant graph belongs to $C_1=Z$, for which $wdeg(C_1)=d$ and $C_{1,Z}=1$. Its factorwise loss is zero. Also $Q=0$ agrees with $f$ on $ep$ points, a fraction $e/p>\u03b5$.\n\n**[P9] (proved: cubic-scale choice).** Assume $p\u22658d$ and set\n\n$$\ne=ceil((dp\u00b2)^{1/3}),\\qquad D=d+e.\n$$\n\nThen $e\u22654d$, $e\u2264p/2+1$, and $D<p$. Since $(dp\u00b2)^{1/3}\u2264e\u22642(dp\u00b2)^{1/3}$ and $p\u2264p+1\u22642p$,\n\n$$\nfrac12(d/p)^{1/3}\u2264\u03b5\u22642(d/p)^{1/3}.\n$$\n\nMoreover $D=\u0398(e)=\u0398(\u03b5p)$, while\n\n$$\ndp/\u03b5=dp(p+1)/e=\u0398(e\u00b2).\n$$\n\nThus $D=\u0398(sqrt(dp/\u03b5))$. Every exponent manipulation in the sharpness claim is contained in these displayed comparisons.\n\n**[P10] (refuted: minimum-interpolant saturation).** The construction does not prove that KTZ's chosen minimum-weight interpolant pays the whole-$B$ loss. The polynomial $Z$, of weight $d<D$, already vanishes on every selected nonvertical graph and has derivative one. The construction refutes only a cleanup theorem based on an arbitrary primitive squarefree whole relation and its degree data.\n\n**[P11] (refuted as campaign obstructions: inseparability and direction concentration).** The primitive squarefree polynomial $Z^p-X$ has zero vertical derivative, but weighted degree $pd$ and is excluded by $\u03b4<p$. If correct labels are instead concentrated in exactly $k$ direction classes with $f=0$, the exact local agreement is $k/(p+1)$ and $Q=0$ agrees everywhere. Neither example refutes the factorwise theorem or the soundness benchmark.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| KTZ pruning | $\u03b5$ | constants | degree $\u0398(\u03b5p)$ |\n| KTZ selector | degree $\u0398(\u03b5p)$ | $|R|=O(p/\u03b5)$ | one inverse $\u03b5$ |\n| Interpolation | $D\u00b3/d$ coefficients vs. $|R|D$ equations | square root | $D=O(sqrt(dp/\u03b5))$ |\n| Identity and lifting | $D$ versus $\u0398(\u03b5p)$ roots | $D=O(\u03b5p)$ | $\u03b5\u00b3=\u03a9(d/p)$ |\n| Ordinary resultant | $D\u00b2$ exceptional lines | $D\u00b2/p\u00b2$ | only the weaker square-root gate |\n| Weighted resultant | $D\u00b2/d$ exceptional lines | $D\u00b2/(dp\u00b2)=O(1/(\u03b5p))$ | lower order |\n| Whole polar | $D-d$ roots per line | $\u03c4(D-d)/p$ | can equal all of $\u03b5$ |\n| Factor polar | factor weights $\u03b3_i$ | $sum_i\u03c4_i\u03b3_i/p$ | potentially smaller, but conditional |\n| Factor component | minimum degree $k$ | one mixing Cauchy\u2013Schwarz loss | agreement $k/(4p)$ |\n| Sharpness scaling | $e\u00b3\u2248dp\u00b2$ | $\u03b5=e/(p+1)$ | existing exponent $1/3$ exactly |\n| Final benchmark | cubic hypothesis | constant $1/8000$ | one degree-$d$ polynomial |\n\nNo Markov inequality, probabilistic union bound, or interpolation-multiplicity assumption appears in Theorem A or C. KTZ's selector uses Chernoff, a union bound, and Chebyshev, but those introduce constants rather than another power of $\u03b5$. Every sharpness root has local intersection multiplicity exactly one.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\nTheorem C is a successful obstruction to improving the unfactored polar-root budget by B\u00e9zout or multiplicity accounting alone. It is deliberately not a soundness counterexample: it contains the explicit factor and decoder $Z=0$.\n\nThe construction also shows why replacing incidence counts by counts of singular base points is invalid. Each of the $ep$ singular lifted points supports $p$ accepted graph incidences. The resultant/discriminant is proportional to $H\u00b2$; passing to its reduced support $H=0$ loses precisely this concurrency information.\n\nThe attempted stronger conclusion about KTZ's minimum interpolant is refuted in [P10]. A genuine lower bound for that architecture must force several factors to be used by different graph lines while preventing a lower-weight content or factor relation.\n\nThe inseparability and concentrated-direction attempts are disposed of in [P11]. At the legal lower boundary, $p=1009,d=101,e=469,D=570$ realizes the cubic-scale construction. At the extreme near-p boundary $p=103,d=101$, $D<p$ forces $D<2d$, so this quadratic branch-collision construction cannot occur.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The field is exactly $F_p$, and $d\u2265101$ makes $p$ odd.\n- The precise derivative requirement is $deg_Z(C_i)<p$; $\u03b4<p$ is a convenient sufficient hypothesis inherited from KTZ.\n- Primitivity excludes base-only factors. Factorization is over $F_p$, not its algebraic closure.\n- The resultant is never normalized to a discriminant and no leading coefficient is inverted.\n- Local multiplicities are orders in $F_p[t]$; no factorial is inverted.\n- The conditional lift divides only by a nonzero value of $C_{i,Z}$.\n- Content removal is not hidden: Theorem A starts after it, with primitive positive-$Z$-degree $B$.\n- Every sharpness root is distinct and simple. Repeated interpolation nodes or hidden Hasse multiplicities play no role.\n- At $d>p/2$, $\u03b4<p$ permits only one $Z$-dependent factor of $Z$-degree one. At $d=p-1,\u03b4=d$, its derivative is constant.\n- Constant labels in Theorem C are legal under the ambient degree cap $d\u2265101$ and do not analyze the excluded degree-zero regime.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe factorwise lemma does not prove that one factor class retains minimum degree $\u03a9(\u03b5p)$. Lines assigned to different factors may meet at accepted points, and factorwise simplicity does not by itself propagate one polynomial across such a transition. A factor-consistency or list-to-single argument is still required.\n\nIn the worst case an active irreducible factor may have $\u03b3_i=\u0398(D-d)$, so the factorwise bound returns the original cubic gate. Independently, KTZ identity extension requires $D=O(\u03b5p)$ before the cleanup stage. Improving ramification alone therefore cannot improve the benchmark.\n\nThe sharpness construction is reducible and is not minimum-weight for its graph family. It proves exact sharpness only for black-box whole-relation cleanup. It neither proves that KTZ's selected interpolant saturates the loss nor refutes any exponent-$1-o(1)$ soundness theorem.\n\nNo finite computation is used to prove an asymptotic statement, and no claim concerns dimensions above two, extension fields, altered sampling, or individual degree.",

First, for every prime \\(p\\) and every campaign degree \\(101\\le d<p\\), there is a deterministic legal table with local agreement \\(\\epsilon=d/p\\), accepted degree exactly \\(d\\) on every affine line, accepted degree \\(d\\) or \\(d+1\\) at every point, and acceptance supported on all lines. Any fractional family of lines that reaches a fixed fraction \\(\\theta\\) of the accepted points of every target line through *other* accepted lines has total weight \\(\\Theta(p/\\epsilon)\\), with a multiplicative gap at most \\((d+1)/(d-1)\\). Thus the \\(p/\\epsilon\\) scale cannot be improved by a universal graph-theoretic cover, even with exact near-regularity and fractional weights.\n\nSecond, for every table of agreement \\(\\epsilon\\), the probability that two uniformly chosen distinct lines through a uniform point are both accepted there is exactly\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon^2-\\frac{\\epsilon(1-\\epsilon)}p+\n\\frac{\\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)},\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(a_x\\) is the accepted degree of \\(x\\). The lower bound is attained by accepting exactly \\(k\\) direction classes. Hence the usual \\(\\epsilon^2\\) collision loss is sharp.\n\nBoth extremal tables have the obvious global polynomial \\(Q=0\\). An exact primary-source audit also shows that KTZ already uses the affine Vinh estimate, while the stronger Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw bounds do not give the linear component size needed for global agreement in their characteristic ranges. The unconditional benchmark exponent remains \\(1/3\\).\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nFix a prime \\(p\\), an integer \\(101\\le d<p\\), and dimension \\(m=2\\). Let \\(\\mathcal L\\) be the \\(p(p+1)\\) affine lines of \\(\\mathbb F_p^2\\). Every line has \\(p\\) points and every point lies on \\(p+1\\) lines.\n\nA point table is \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\). Each \\(L\\in\\mathcal L\\) has one polynomial label \\(P_L\\) of degree at most \\(d\\), interpreted using a fixed affine parameterization of \\(L\\). Put\n\n\\[\nA(x,L)=1_{\\{P_L(x)=f(x)\\}},\\qquad\n\\epsilon=\\frac{\\sum_{x,L\\ni x}A(x,L)}{p^2(p+1)}.\n\\]\n\nThis is exactly uniform-line-then-uniform-point sampling. Let\n\n\\[\na_x=\\sum_{L\\ni x}A(x,L),\\qquad\nN_E(L)=\\{x\\in L:A(x,L)=1\\}.\n\\]\n\nFor nonnegative line weights \\(\\lambda=(\\lambda_M)_{M\\in\\mathcal L}\\), define the capped load reaching an accepted incidence \\((x,L)\\) through other lines by\n\n\\[\nu_{x,L}(\\lambda)=\n\\min\\left\\{1,\\sum_{\\substack{M\\ni x,\\,M\\ne L}}A(x,M)\\lambda_M\\right\\}.\n\\]\n\nFor \\(0<\\theta\\le1\\), call \\(\\lambda\\) \\(\\theta\\)-reaching if\n\n\\[\n\\sum_{x\\in N_E(L)}u_{x,L}(\\lambda)\\ge\\theta |N_E(L)|\n\\quad\\text{for every }L\\in\\mathcal L.\n\\]\n\nIndicator weights are ordinary selected-line families. Fractional weights also cover multisets after coincident copies are combined.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe active corpus contains four earlier submissions and four verifier audits. Researcher-0002 is the only accepted result: a connected accepted component of minimum degree \\(k\\) and line measure \\(\\tau\\) is decoded under \\(k^2\\ge2^{40}dp\\) and \\(k^3\\ge2^{40}d\\tau p^2\\), giving a conditional exponent \\(1/2\\) when \\(\\tau=O(\\epsilon)\\). The data manifest is a launch snapshot and is not current mathematical evidence; the live boards and audits control this synthesis.\n\nThe benchmark is [Kominers\u2013Thaler\u2013Zheng, Revision 1, Theorem 1.1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/): over every finite field, agreement \\(\\epsilon\\ge C(d/q)^{1/3}\\) yields one total-degree-at-most-\\(d\\) polynomial with global agreement \\(c\\epsilon\\). Their Theorem 4 additionally treats a genuine Cartesian set \\(A\\times B\\), under \\(|A|\\le|B|\\), \\(|A||B|^2\\le|T|^3\\), and \\(|A||T|\\ll p^2\\). These hypotheses cannot be silently imposed on accepted-point supports. Bourgain\u2013Katz\u2013Tao Theorem 6.2 has an unspecified gain depending on a fixed support exponent and is not used.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A (regular carrier and other-line fractional-cover obstruction).** Let \\(p\\) be prime and let \\(101\\le d<p\\). There exist \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\) and degree-exactly-\\(d\\) labels \\(P_L\\), one for every affine line, such that:\n\n1. \\(|N_E(L)|=d\\) for every \\(L\\), while \\(a_x\\in\\{d,d+1\\}\\) for every \\(x\\). Exactly \\(pd\\) points have degree \\(d+1\\), and the remaining \\(p(p-d)\\) points have degree \\(d\\).\n2. The agreement is \\(\\epsilon=d/p\\), and every affine line supports acceptance.\n3. The total-degree-zero polynomial \\(Q=0\\) satisfies \\(Q(x)=f(x)\\) for every point.\n\n**Lemma B (exact two-line collision identity).** For any valid table in the same ambient regime, let \\(\\Gamma_2\\) be the probability that, after choosing \\(x\\) uniformly and an ordered pair \\((L,M)\\) of distinct lines through \\(x\\) uniformly, both \\((x,L)\\) and \\((x,M)\\) accept. For each \\(b\\in\\mathbb F_p\\), connect dummy vertex \\(z_b\\) to the \\(p\\) lines \\(y=mx+b\\), \\(m\\in\\mathbb F_p\\), and to the vertical line \\(x=b\\). The resulting bipartite graph has \\(p(p+1)\\) vertices on each side and is \\((p+1)\\)-regular. A regular bipartite graph has a perfect matching: for every left set \\(S\\), its \\((p+1)|S|\\) edges enter at most \\((p+1)|N(S)|\\) slots, so Hall's condition holds. Removing a perfect matching preserves regularity. Iteration decomposes the augmented graph into \\(p+1\\) perfect matchings, regarded as colors.\n\nAfter deleting the dummy edges, every real point sees every color exactly once. Every affine line misses exactly the color of its unique dummy edge. Each color is absent from exactly \\(p\\) affine lines because its perfect matching contains exactly one edge at each of the \\(p\\) dummy vertices.\n\n**[P2] (proved: select and repair colors).** Select any \\(d\\) colors and let \\(E_0\\) be their real incidence edges. Every point has \\(E_0\\)-degree \\(d\\). A line has degree \\(d\\) unless its missing color was selected, in which case it has degree \\(d-1\\). There are exactly \\(pd\\) distinct deficient lines.\n\nPut \\(r=p+1-d>0\\). In the graph of unselected real incidences from deficient lines to real points, every deficient line has degree \\(r\\), while every point has degree at most \\(r\\). Hence for every deficient-line set \\(S\\),\n\n\\[\nr|S|=e(S,N(S))\\le r|N(S)|.\n\\]\n\nHall gives a matching saturating all deficient lines. Add these matching edges to \\(E_0\\). Every line now has degree \\(d\\); the \\(pd\\) distinct matching endpoints have point degree \\(d+1\\), and all other points retain degree \\(d\\).\n\n**[P3] (proved: realize the accepted graph).** Set \\(f=0\\). A nonzero interpolant therefore requires $D^3/d$ to dominate $|R|D$, or $D^2\u2273d|R|$. The source chooses $D=16(floor(sqrt(d|R|))+1)$, yielding the displayed bound. This coefficient count is an exponent reconstruction from KTZ's parameters.\n\n**[P4 \u2014 proved] The cubic coupling.** Dividing the displayed upper bound by $\u03b5p$ gives\n\n$D/(\u03b5p)\u22641280(sqrt(\u03c1/\u03b5^3)+1/(\u03b5p))$.\n\nLemma 4.3 needs $D<k_0/2$ to turn more than $D$ distinct covered roots on a line into a formal identity. Section 5 loses normalized incidence mass\n\n$D/p+D^2/[p(p+1)]$,\n\nwhose first term must be $O(\u03b5)$. Lemma 6.1 again needs $D<k_1/2$ to obtain more than $D$ incident line roots. Each dominant requirement therefore asks $\u03c1/\u03b5^3=O(1)$, namely $\u03b5\u2273\u03c1^{1/3}$. By contrast, the quadratic deletion term is $O(\u03c1/\u03b5)$ and asks only $\u03c1=O(\u03b5^2)$.\n\n**[P5 \u2014 proved] Probability and constant-loss audit.** In the source bookkeeping, popularity averaging charges at most $\u03b5/2$ to low-popularity incidences; the first degree pruning charges less than $\u03b5/50$ and retains at least $\u03b5/4$. Lemma 3.2 uses a Chernoff bound for each line's coverage, a union bound over $p(p+1)$ lines, and a second-moment/Chebyshev bound for $|R|$; its parameter lemma ensures $\u03b5p\u226blog p$. Section 5 charges exactly $D/p+D^2/[p(p+1)]\u2264\u03b5/16$. The second pruning charges less than $\u03b5/16$ and leaves edge measure at least $\u03b5/8$. Lemma 2.1 is the sole incidence Cauchy\u2013Schwarz loss, with normalized error at most $sqrt(\u03bc(X)\u03bc(T)/(p+1))$; the imposed $p^{-1/2}\u2264\u03b5/8000$ yields component measures at least $\u03b5/8000$. There is no additional Markov loss in KTZ. Thus no suppressed power of $\u03c1$ occurs after [P4].\n\n**[P6 \u2014 proved] A good line at d=0.** Choose $f(x)$ independently and uniformly from $F_p$. On a fixed line let $N_a$ be the occupancy of color $a$ and let $Y=sum_a 1[N_a=r]$. With\n\n$a_0=Pr[N_a=r]=binom(p,r)p^{-r}(1-1/p)^{p-r}$,\n\nthe assumptions on $p$ give\n\n$prod_{i=0}^{r-1}(1-i/p)\u22651-r(r-1)/(2p)\u22651/2$\n\nand $(1-1/p)^{p-r}\u2265(1-1/p)^p\u22651/4$. Hence $a_0\u22651/(8r!)$ and $E[Y]=pa_0\u22651$. For distinct colors,\n\n$Pr[N_a=N_b=r]\u22641/(r!)^2\u226464a_0^2$.\n\nTherefore $E[Y^2]\u2264E[Y]+64E[Y]^2\u226465E[Y]^2$. The second-moment inequality gives $Pr[Y>0]\u22651/65$.\n\n**[P7 \u2014 proved] Simultaneous global balance.** Let $g(f)$ be the fraction of lines with $Y>0$, so $E[g]\u22651/65$. For a fixed color, its total occupancy in the plane is $Bin(p^2,1/p)$ with mean $p$. Chernoff and a union bound over all $p$ colors give\n\n$Pr[max_a |f^{-1}(a)|>2p]\u2264p(e/4)^p\u2264pe^{-p/3}\u22641/130$.\n\nIf $H$ is the complementary event, then $E[g1_H]\u22651/65-1/130=1/130$. Thus some $f$ satisfies $H$ and $g(f)\u22651/130$. On each good line choose a color occurring exactly $r$ times and use it as the constant $P_L$; label other lines arbitrarily. This gives $Acc\u2265r/(130p)$, while $H$ gives $Agr_0\u22642/p$. Independence between different lines was never assumed.\n\n**[P8 \u2014 refuted] Universal soundness over 0\u2264d<p.** If an absolute conclusion $Agr_0\u2265c Acc$ held, [P7] would imply $c\u2264260/r$ for every $r$. Choosing $r>260/c$ is a contradiction. The threshold constant $C$ cannot repair this because its threshold is identically zero at $d=0$.\n\n**[P9 \u2014 proved] Random incidence graph.** Retain every affine point-line incidence independently with probability $\u03b4$. Chernoff bounds and a union bound over fewer than $3p^2$ point and line vertices show, with probability greater than $3/4$ under the stated hypothesis, that every point and line has degree at least $\u03b4p/2$ and every line has degree at most $2\u03b4p$.\n\n**[P10 \u2014 proved] No small reaching family.** Fix $R$ with $r\u2264r_0=floor(p/(64\u03b4))$. Some parallel class contains at most $r/(p+1)$ lines of $R$, leaving at least $p/2$ test lines outside $R$. For such a line $L$, let $n_x$ count lines of $R$ through $x\u2208L$. Then $sum_x n_x\u2264r$. The coverage indicators at distinct $x$ are independent and\n\n$E[cov_R(L)]\u2264\u03b4 sum_x[1-(1-\u03b4)^{n_x}]\u2264\u03b4^2r\u2264\u03b4p/64$.\n\nConsequently\n\n$Pr[cov_R(L)>\u03b4p/4]\u2264(e/16)^{\u03b4p/4}$.\n\nFor distinct parallel test lines the relevant incidence variables are disjoint, so the probability that this fixed $R$ reaches all of them is at most $exp(-\u03b4p^2/32)$. The number of sets of at most $r_0$ lines is at most\n\n$exp((p/(64\u03b4))log(256ep))\u2264exp(\u03b4p^2/4096)$.\n\nA union bound gives probability less than $1/4$ that any small $R$ succeeds. Intersecting with [P9] proves Theorem C.\n\n**[P11 \u2014 proved] Exact polynomial realization.** Fix the line parameterizations and let $S_L\u2286F_p$ be the retained parameters on $L$. Set $f=0$ and\n\n$P_L(t)=prod_{a\u2208S_L}(t-a)$.\n\nThen $P_L(t)=f(ell_L(t))$ exactly on the retained incidences. Its degree is $|S_L|\u22642\u03b4p<p$. The line-degree bounds give $\u03b1\u2208[\u03b4/2,2\u03b4]$, and $p/(64\u03b4)\u2265p/(128\u03b1)$. Since the global polynomial $Q=0$ agrees everywhere, this is only an obstruction to incidence-only sparsification.\n\n**[P12 \u2014 proved] Local agreement in the positive-degree adversary.** Before sampling $f$, fix $d+1$ points $S_L$ on every line. Sample $f$ independently and uniformly, and let $P_L$ be the unique degree-at-most-$d$ interpolant through $f|_{S_L}$. The selected points always agree. At every other point of $L$, $P_L(x)$ is determined by $f|_{S_L}$ and is independent of $f(x)$, so\n\n$E[Acc]=(d+1)/p+(p-d-1)/p^2\u2264(d+2)/p$.\n\nEvery outcome has $Acc\u2265(d+1)/p$, while Markov gives $Pr[Acc>4(d+2)/p]\u22641/4$.\n\n**[P13 \u2014 proved] Global union bound.** There are $p^K$ formal total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials, where $K=(d+1)(d+2)/2$. For fixed $Q$, its number of agreements with random $f$ is $Bin(p^2,1/p)$ with mean $p$. If $T\u2264p^2$, Chernoff and a union bound give\n\n$Pr[exists Q: agreements(Q)\u2265T]\u2264p^K(ep/T)^T\u2264p^K(e/4)^T\u2264p^{-(4log4-5)K}<1/4$.\n\nIf $T>p^2$, the event is empty. Thus with positive probability the Markov-good event in [P12] and this global-good event occur simultaneously, proving Proposition D.\n\n**[P14 \u2014 proved] Sharp-scale specialization.** For $d=floor(sqrt(p/log p))$, one has $K log p=O(p)$ and hence $T=O(p)$. In fact $T\u226413p$ for all sufficiently large $p$. Therefore $Agr_d\u226413/p$, while $Acc\u2265(d+1)/p$, so the ratio is at most $13/(d+1)\u21920$.\n\n**[P15 \u2014 conditional] What sparsification alone could buy.** Suppose a replacement for Lemma 3.2 gave $|R|=O(p/\u03b5^\u03b3)$ while retaining the same coefficient-count and root-budget steps. Then\n\n$D^2\u2273dp/\u03b5^\u03b3$ and $D\u2272\u03b5p$\n\nimply $d/p\u2272\u03b5^{2+\u03b3}$, or $\u03b5\u2273\u03c1^{1/(2+\u03b3)}$. Thus $|R|=O(p)$ gives exponent $1/2$, not exponent near one. Near-linear soundness needs a family near the geometric scale $\u0398(\u03b5p)$ or a different interpolation/propagation mechanism. Theorem C shows that density and minimum degree alone cannot even provide $O(p)$ on all accepted graphs.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Pruning | $\u03b5$ | absolute constants | edge measure $\u2265\u03b5/4$, $k_0=\u0398(\u03b5p)$ |\n| Sparsification | $k_0=\u0398(\u03b5p)$ | one factor $\u03b5^{-1}$ | $|R|=O(p/\u03b5)$ |\n| Interpolation | $dim(V_D)=\u03a9(D^3/d)$, $O(|R|D)$ constraints | square root | $D=O(sqrt(dp/\u03b5)+1)$ |\n| Root extension | $D<k_0/2$ | compare with $\u03b5p$ | $\u03b5^3\u2273d/p$ |\n| Trivial-line deletion | $D/p\u2264O(\u03b5)$ | compare with $\u03b5p$ | $\u03b5^3\u2273d/p$ |\n| Degenerate-line deletion | $D^2/p^2\u2264O(\u03b5)$ | quadratic term | $\u03b5^2\u2273d/p$ only |\n| Root lifting | $D<k_1/2$ | compare with $\u03b5p$ | $\u03b5^3\u2273d/p$ |\n| Formal-degree safety | $D<p$ | none beyond degree | $\u03b5\u2273d/p$ only |\n| Chernoff and mixing | $\u03b5p$, $p^{-1/2}$ | logarithmic/field-size conditions | no new $d/p$ power |\n| Propagation | one $G_1$ component | factor $1/8000$ | global agreement $\u2265\u03b5/8000$ |\n| Hypothetical $|R|=O(p/\u03b5^\u03b3)$ | same algebra | architecture conversion | exponent $1/(2+\u03b3)$ |\n| Endpoint $d=0$ | threshold zero | ratio $\u2264260/r$ | universal linear conclusion refuted |\n| Sharp-scale adversary | $\u03b5=\u0398(d/p)$ | global $O(1/p)$ | ratio $O(1/d)$ |\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Degree zero \u2014 successful.** Theorem A is a genuine counterexample to the literal target, not merely to a proof technique.\n\n2. **Random prescribed interpolation \u2014 scale obstruction.** Proposition D shows that agreement of order $d/p$ cannot by itself force a constant global/local ratio. Its agreement is far below $(d/p)^{1/3}$, so it does not challenge KTZ.\n\n3. **Diffuse random incidences \u2014 proof-method obstruction.** Theorem C matches the $p/\u03b5$ reaching-family size, but its realization has the perfect decoder $Q=0$ and $d_G=\u0398(\u03b5p)$. It cannot rule out a sparsifier exploiting the stronger cubic-regime inequality $d\u226a\u03b5p$.\n\n4. **Concentrated good directions \u2014 not extremal.** If about $\u03b5p$ whole direction classes are accepted, one complete parallel class of $p$ lines reaches every point. This replaces $p/\u03b5$ by $p$ and leads to the exponent-$1/2$ ledger, so concentration is easier than the diffuse graph.\n\n5. **Near-characteristic degree \u2014 nonvacuousness failure.** At $d=p-1$, arbitrary restrictions can be interpolated on every line. After enlarging the existential KTZ constant to $C\u22651$, however, $\u03b5\u2265C(d/p)^{1/3}$ is generally impossible near $d=p$, so this does not refute the published positive-degree statement.\n\n6. **Small fields \u2014 exact checks only.** Exhaustive enumeration at $(p,d)=(2,0),(2,1),(3,0),(3,1),(3,2)$ found worst local/global ratios $4/3,4/3,7/4,3/2,9/7$, respectively. These checks expose no additional positive-degree defect and carry no asymptotic force.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\nFor $1\u2264d<p$, the positive-degree proof is characteristic-safe. KTZ's allowed monomials omit positive $Z^k$ with $p|k$; once $D<p$, this omission is automatic because $k\u2264D/d<p$. The minimum-weight interpolant is squarefree. Since finite fields are perfect, an irreducible factor with all ordinary partial derivatives zero would be a nontrivial $p$-th power. Lemma 2.4 then chooses an $F_p$-directional derivative outside fewer than $p$ bad subspaces; this is where the strict $D<p$ matters.\n\nRevision 1 uses no discriminant and assumes no absolute irreducibility. Coprimality of $B$ and its directional derivative is sufficient for the resultant count. The factorization $A=HB$ is exact; cancellation is in $F_p[t]$, not pointwise division by $H$. After derivative-degenerate incidences are removed, $B_Z(x,f(x))$ is a nonzero field element. Newton\u2013Hensel lifting divides only by this scalar and uses no factorials. All interpolation uses ordinary coefficient constraints and distinct roots, not hidden multiplicities.\n\nAt $d=0$, by contrast, the weighted $Z$-degree is zero, Lemma 2.2's dimension bound divides by $d$, and the minimum-weight argument loses positivity. Theorem A shows that this is a genuine theorem-level defect rather than harmless notation.\n\n## Limitations\n\n- No exponent stronger than $1/3$ is proved for the corrected regime $1\u2264d<p$; therefore `benchmark_improved=false`.\n- The endpoint counterexample corrects the literal campaign statement. It should not be presented as refuting KTZ if that paper's intended convention is $d\u22651$.\n- The reaching-set obstruction applies to arguments using only incidence density and minimum degree. Its polynomial realization has a perfect global decoder and lies at $d=\u0398(\u03b5p)$, not in the cubic regime.\n- Proposition D confirms the $d/p$ scale only up to constants; it does not rule out a theorem triggered at every sufficiently large constant multiple of $d/p$.\n- Revision 1 does not publish an explicit valid threshold constant $C$, so this audit preserves its existential constant rather than importing the old cached value.\n- Finite enumeration was used only for falsification. It cannot establish asymptotic soundness.\n- No claim is made about dimensions above two, extension fields, descent, or dimension bootstrapping.",

research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0009/response.json:155:  "note_markdown": "# Sharp Higher-Moment Envelopes and Raw-DRC Barriers for Good Affine Incidences\n\n## Abstract\n\nFix a prime $p$, an integer $101\\le d<p$, and dimension $m=2$. I prove sharp all-order lower bounds for point-centered and line-centered distinct-star moments of the accepted-incidence graph. The bounds are the adjacent-integer convex envelopes of falling factorials. I then give an explicit legal line-versus-point table at local agreement $\\epsilon_0=d/p$ whose accepted graph is connected, has full point and line support, and attains both families of moment bounds simultaneously for every admissible order. On the same table, every fractional family that reaches a $\\theta$ fraction of the accepted points of every line through other accepted lines has weight $\\Theta(\\theta p/\\epsilon_0)$, with exact bounds differing by at most $1.02$.\n\nEvery affine point-line incidence graph is $K_{2,2}$-free, so ordinary common-neighborhood dependent random choice on the raw accepted graph cannot produce a nontrivial biclique. I also prove an exact higher-moment DRC certificate for the auxiliary line-compatibility graph, including a concurrency correction that counts target lines receiving genuinely distinct intersection roots. Its acceptance-density-only specialization pays $\\epsilon^{2t}$ at moment order $t$; direct insertion into KTZ interpolation needs $t>256d$ and is therefore much worse than the cubic route.\n\nThese results isolate a proof-architecture barrier, not a soundness counterexample. The explicit extremizer has $f=0$, and the single total-degree-zero polynomial $Q=0$ agrees globally everywhere. Accordingly, the unconditional exponent-$1/3$ benchmark is not improved.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nLet $\\mathcal L$ be the $p(p+1)$ affine lines of $\\mathbb F_p^2$. Each line contains $p$ points and each point lies on $p+1$ lines. A valid table consists of\n\n$$\nf:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p,\n\\qquad\nP_L\\in\\mathbb F_p[t],\\quad \\deg P_L\\le d\\quad(L\\in\\mathcal L),\n$$\n\nusing a fixed affine parameterization of each line. Put\n\n$$\nE=\\{(x,L):x\\in L,\\ P_L(x)=f(x)\\},\n\\qquad\n\\epsilon=\\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)}.\n$$\n\nThis is exactly uniform affine-line sampling followed by a uniform point of the line. Because the incidence graph is biregular, it is equivalently a uniform point followed by a uniform incident line. Define accepted degrees\n\n$$\na_x=|\\{L\\ni x:(x,L)\\in E\\}|,\n\\qquad\nb_L=|\\{x\\in L:(x,L)\\in E\\}|.\n$$\n\nFor integers $u,s\\ge0$, let $(u)_s=u(u-1)\\cdots(u-s+1)$, with $(u)_0=1$. For $\\mu\\in[0,n]$, write $k=\\lfloor\\mu\\rfloor$ and $\\rho=\\mu-k$, and define the adjacent-integer interpolation\n\n$$\nJ_s(\\mu)=(1-\\rho)(k)_s+\\rho(k+1)_s.\n$$\n\nFor $0\\le s\\le p+1$, let $\\Gamma_s^P$ be the probability that, after choosing uniform $x$, an ordered $s$-tuple of distinct lines through $x$ consists entirely of accepted incidences. For $0\\le s\\le p$, define $\\Gamma_s^L$ analogously by choosing a uniform line and an ordered $s$-tuple of distinct points on it. Tildes, as in $\\widetilde\\Gamma_s^P$, denote independent sampling with replacement.\n\nFor fractional reaching, let $\\lambda_M\\ge0$ be line weights and set\n\n$$\nu_{x,L}(\\lambda)=\n\\min\\left\\{1,\n\\sum_{\\substack{M\\ni x,\\ M\\ne L\\\\(x,M)\\in E}}\\lambda_M\n\\right\\}.\n$$\n\nThe weights are $\\theta$-reaching if\n\n$$\n\\sum_{x:(x,L)\\in E}u_{x,L}(\\lambda)\\ge\\theta b_L\n$$\n\nfor every line $L$, where $0<\\theta\\le1$. Let $\\operatorname{OPT}_\\theta$ be the minimum of $\\sum_M\\lambda_M$.\n\nFinally, the auxiliary compatibility graph $H$ has vertex set $\\mathcal L$. Distinct lines are adjacent when they are nonparallel and both accept at their unique intersection.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe benchmark is [Kominers--Thaler--Zheng, Revision 1, Theorem 1.1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/): over every finite field, acceptance $\\epsilon\\ge C(d/q)^{1/3}$ yields one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with global agreement at least $c\\epsilon$. Only its $m=2$, $q=p$ specialization is used here.\n\nThe following exponent explanation is my reconstruction, not a quoted KTZ theorem. KTZ Lemma 3.2 selects $|R|=O(p/\\epsilon)$ lines. Lemmas 2.2 and 4.1--4.2 give a weighted-degree explainer\n\n$$\nD=O\\!\\left(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon}\\right).\n$$\n\nLemma 4.3 and the lifting step require $D=O(\\epsilon p)$. Hence\n\n$$\n\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon}=O(\\epsilon p)\n\\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p).\n$$\n\nThe active verifier board accepts two earlier results. Researcher-0002 proves a component-sensitive decoder and a conditional exponent $1/2$ when a pruned component has line measure $O(\\epsilon)$. Researcher-0006 isolates singular lifted incidences as an algebraic obstruction. Researchers 0001, 0004, 0005, 0007, and 0008 are revise-grade; researcher-0003's exact aggregate theorem was rejected for omitted interpolation hypotheses. In particular, researcher-0004 proves uniform interpolation multiplicity exponent-neutral, while researcher-0008 proves the exact second collision identity and a nearly regular carrier. The present note independently re-proves and strengthens the latter to every moment order, gives a simpler explicit carrier, and proves that its accepted graph is connected. The live leaderboards, rather than the launch-time data manifest, determine these statuses.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem 1 (sharp raw moments and a connected simultaneous extremizer).** Fix a prime $p$ and $101\\le d<p$.\n\n1. For every valid table of agreement $\\epsilon$,\n\n$$\n\\Gamma_s^P=\n\\frac{\\mathbb E_x[(a_x)_s]}{(p+1)_s}\n\\ge\n\\frac{J_s((p+1)\\epsilon)}{(p+1)_s}\n\\qquad(0\\le s\\le p+1),\n$$\n\nand\n\n$$\n\\Gamma_s^L=\n\\frac{\\mathbb E_L[(b_L)_s]}{(p)_s}\n\\ge\n\\frac{J_s(p\\epsilon)}{(p)_s}\n\\qquad(0\\le s\\le p).\n$$\n\nFor every integer $r\\ge1$,\n\n$$\n\\widetilde\\Gamma_r^P\\ge\\epsilon^r,\n\\qquad\n\\widetilde\\Gamma_r^L\\ge\\epsilon^r.\n$$\n\n2. There is an explicit legal table with $\\epsilon_0=d/p$ such that its accepted graph is connected,\n\n$$\nb_L=d\\quad\\text{for every }L,\n$$\n\nand\n\n$$\na_x=\n\\begin{cases}\nd+1,&\\text{at exactly }pd\\text{ points},\\\\\nd,&\\text{at exactly }p(p-d)\\text{ points}.\n\\end{cases}\n$$\n\nIt simultaneously attains both distinct-star lower envelopes for every admissible $s$:\n\n$$\n\\Gamma_s^P=\n\\frac{(1-d/p)(d)_s+(d/p)(d+1)_s}{(p+1)_s},\n\\qquad\n\\Gamma_s^L=\\frac{(d)_s}{(p)_s}.\n$$\n\nIts line-centered with-replacement moments equal $\\epsilon_0^r$ for every $r\\ge1$.\n\n3. On this table, for every $0<\\theta\\le1$,\n\n$$\n\\frac{\\theta p(p+1)}{d+1}\n\\le\\operatorname{OPT}_\\theta\n\\le\n\\frac{\\theta p(p+1)}{d-1}.\n$$\n\n4. Every accepted affine point-line graph is $K_{2,2}$-free. Thus two or more distinct vertices sampled from either shore have at most one common neighbor on the other shore.\n\nThe constructed table has $f=0$, and $Q=0$ has global agreement one.\n\n**Theorem 2 (auxiliary compatibility-graph DRC with concurrency correction).** For any valid table, let $N=p(p+1)$, $\\mu=(p+1)\\epsilon$, and let $\\bar\\Delta$ be the average degree of $H$. Then\n\n$$\ne(H)=\\sum_x\\binom{a_x}{2},\n\\qquad\n\\bar\\Delta\\ge\\frac{p\\mu(\\mu-1)}{p+1}.\n$$\n\nFor every integer $1\\le t\\le\\lfloor\\bar\\Delta\\rfloor$, define\n\n$$\nM_t(H)=\n\\frac{\\sum_{L\\in\\mathcal L}\\binom{\\deg_H(L)}t}{\\binom Nt}.\n$$\n\nThere is a set $S$ of $t$ distinct seed lines with at least $M_t(H)$ common neighbors. If $1\\le h\\le t$ and $h_L$ is the number of distinct points among $\\{L\\cap M:M\\in S\\}$, then the same $S$ has at least\n\n$$\nM_t(H)-\n\\frac{\\binom t2(p+1)}{t-h+1}\n$$\n\ncommon-neighbor lines satisfying $h_L\\ge h$. Moreover,\n\n$$\nM_t(H)\\ge\nN\\frac{\\binom{\\lfloor\\bar\\Delta\\rfloor}t}{\\binom Nt}.\n$$\n\nIf $\\mu\\ge2$ and $\\bar\\Delta\\ge2t+2$, the last expression is at least $N(\\epsilon^2/4)^t$.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n### [P1] \u2014 proved: exact star identities\n\nDouble counting accepted incidences gives\n\n$$\n\\mathbb E_x a_x=(p+1)\\epsilon,\n\\qquad\n\\mathbb E_L b_L=p\\epsilon.\n$$\n\nAt a fixed point $x$, precisely $(a_x)_s$ ordered tuples of $s$ distinct incident lines are wholly accepted, out of $(p+1)_s$. Averaging proves the point identity. The line identity is identical with $b_L$ and $(p)_s$. No independence or concentration estimate is used.\n\n### [P2] \u2014 proved: sharp discrete moment lower envelope\n\nFor $F_s(j)=(j)_s$ on nonnegative integers,\n\n$$\n\\Delta F_s(j)=s(j)_{s-1},\n\\qquad\n\\Delta^2F_s(j)=s(s-1)(j)_{s-2}\\ge0.\n$$\n\nThus the piecewise-linear interpolation of $F_s$ is convex. Jensen gives\n\n$$\n\\mathbb E[(A)_s]\\ge J_s(\\mathbb EA)\n$$\n\nfor every integer-valued degree variable $A$. The minimizer need not be unique when the falling factorial vanishes, but the adjacent-integer mixture always attains the minimum. Applying this to [P1] proves the distinct-star inequalities.\n\nFor sampling with replacement,\n\n$$\n\\widetilde\\Gamma_r^P=\n\\mathbb E_x\\left(\\frac{a_x}{p+1}\\right)^r,\n\\qquad\n\\widetilde\\Gamma_r^L=\n\\mathbb E_L\\left(\\frac{b_L}{p}\\right)^r.\n$$\n\nOrdinary Jensen for $z\\mapsto z^r$ gives the two $\\epsilon^r$ bounds. Repeated samples must not be confused with distinct constraints: $a^r=\\sum_j {r\\brace j}(a)_j$ includes duplicate-line events.\n\n### [P3] \u2014 proved: explicit legal carrier\n\nLet\n\n$$\nS_d=\\{0,1,\\ldots,d-1\\}\\subset\\mathbb F_p\n$$\n\nand set $f(x,y)=0$. For a nonvertical line\n\n$$\nL_{m,b}(t)=(t,mt+b),\n$$\n\nset\n\n$$\nP_{m,b}(t)=\\prod_{s\\in S_d}(t+m-s).\n$$\n\nFor the vertical line $V_c(t)=(c,t)$, set\n\n$$\nP_{V_c}(t)=\\prod_{s\\in S_d}(t-s).\n$$\n\nAll labels have formal degree exactly $d<p$. A nonvertical incidence at $(x,y)$ accepts exactly when $x+m\\in S_d$. Therefore every point has exactly $d$ accepted nonvertical lines, one for each slope $m=s-x$, $s\\in S_d$. Its vertical line also accepts exactly when $y\\in S_d$. Hence the asserted point degrees hold. Every nonvertical line has the $d$ roots $t=s-m$, and every vertical line has the $d$ roots $t=s$. Thus every line degree is $d$.\n\nThere are $dp(p+1)$ accepted incidences, so\n\n$$\n\\epsilon_0=\n\\frac{dp(p+1)}{p^2(p+1)}=\frac dp.\n$$\n\n### [P4] \u2014 proved: connectivity\n\nBecause $d\\ge101$, the elements $0,1,2$ belong to $S_d$. For any $(x,y)$, put\n\n$$\nC=(x-1,y+x-1).\n$$\n\nThe points $(x,y)$ and $C$ lie on a line of slope $1-x$ and have acceptance values $x+(1-x)=1$ and $(x-1)+(1-x)=0$. The points $C$ and $(x,y+1)$ lie on a line of slope $2-x$ and have acceptance values $1$ and $2$. Thus $(x,y)$ and $(x,y+1)$ are joined by a four-edge accepted path.\n\nAlso, $(x,y)$ and $(x+1,y-x)$ share the accepted line of slope $-x$, since their acceptance values are $0$ and $1$. Vertical unit moves connect every point in a fixed column; the second move connects column $x$ to column $x+1$. Since $1$ generates the additive group of the prime field, every point vertex lies in one component. Every line vertex has $d>0$ accepted neighbors, so the full accepted bipartite graph is connected.\n\n### [P5] \u2014 proved: simultaneous moment extremality\n\nFor the carrier,\n\n$$\n(p+1)\\epsilon_0=d+d/p.\n$$\n\nThe point-degree distribution is exactly the adjacent mixture at this mean: degree $d+1$ has probability $d/p=\\epsilon_0$, and degree $d$ has probability $1-\\epsilon_0$. The line mean is $p\\epsilon_0=d$, and every line has that degree. Equality therefore holds in both inequalities of [P2] for every admissible $s$.\n\nIn particular, $\\Gamma_s^L=0$ for $s>d$ and $\\Gamma_s^P=0$ for $s>d+1$. Fixed mean alone cannot manufacture more distinct algebraic constraints than the local degree permits. At $s=2$,\n\n$$\n\\Gamma_2^P=\n\\epsilon_0^2-\n\\frac{\\epsilon_0(1-\\epsilon_0)}{p+1}.\n$$\n\nFor $2\\le s\\le(d+1)/2$,\n\n$$\n2^{-(s-1)}\\epsilon_0^s\n\\le\\frac{(d)_s}{(p)_s}\n\\le\\epsilon_0^s.\n$$\n\nThe exact product, rather than this coarse comparison, is retained in the theorem.\n\n### [P6] \u2014 proved: fractional other-line reaching\n\nWeights may be truncated to $[0,1]$ without changing capped loads; compactness therefore makes the minimum attainable. Put\n\n$$\nv_x=\n\\min\\left\\{1,\n\\sum_{M\\ni x:(x,M)\\in E}\\lambda_M\n\\right\\}.\n$$\n\nSince $u_{x,L}\\le v_x$, any $\\theta$-reaching weights satisfy\n\n$$\n\\theta d\\,p(p+1)\n\\le\\sum_x a_xv_x\n\\le(d+1)\\sum_xv_x\n\\le d(d+1)\\sum_M\\lambda_M.\n$$\n\nThis proves the lower bound. Conversely, assign every line weight $\\theta/(d-1)$. At an accepted incidence, at least $a_x-1\\ge d-1$ other accepted lines occur, so $u_{x,L}\\ge\\theta$. This proves the upper bound. Their ratio is\n\n$$\n\\frac{d+1}{d-1}\\le\\frac{102}{100}.\n$$\n\nSince $d=p\\epsilon_0$, the cost is $\\Theta(\\theta p/\\epsilon_0)$ with explicit constants.\n\n### [P7] \u2014 proved: raw DRC collapse\n\nTwo distinct affine points determine one affine line, and two distinct affine lines meet in at most one point. Hence the full affine incidence graph, and every accepted subgraph, contains no $K_{2,2}$. A common-neighborhood DRC sample containing at least two distinct raw vertices therefore has common neighborhood of size at most one. If sampling with replacement appears to give a large common neighborhood, after deduplication it is either a one-vertex star or has common neighborhood at most one.\n\nThis assertion concerns only the raw point-line graph. Auxiliary compatibility graphs may contain many four-cycles.\n\n### [P8] \u2014 proved: auxiliary edge count\n\nEvery unordered pair of accepted lines through $x$ gives one edge of $H$, and every edge has a unique intersection point. Therefore\n\n$$\ne(H)=\\sum_x\\binom{a_x}{2}.\n$$\n\nSince $N=p(p+1)$,\n\n$$\n\\bar\\Delta=\n\\frac{2e(H)}N\n=\frac{p\\,\\mathbb E_x[a_x(a_x-1)]}{p+1}\n\\ge\\frac{p\\mu(\\mu-1)}{p+1},\n$$\n\nwhere the last step is convexity. The sharper adjacent-integer form follows by replacing $\\mu(\\mu-1)$ with $J_2(\\mu)$.\n\n### [P9] \u2014 proved: exact auxiliary DRC moment\n\nCount pairs $(S,L)$ in which $S$ is a $t$-element subset of $N_H(L)$. Their number is\n\n$$\n\\sum_L\\binom{\\deg_H(L)}t.\n$$\n\nAveraging over the $\\binom Nt$ choices of $S$ gives a seed set with at least $M_t(H)$ common neighbors. Discrete convexity of $j\\mapsto\\binom jt$ gives\n\n$$\nM_t(H)\\ge\nN\\frac{\\binom{\\lfloor\\bar\\Delta\\rfloor}t}{\\binom Nt}.\n$$\n\nIf $\\bar\\Delta\\ge2t+2$, every numerator factor is at least $\\bar\\Delta/2$, so the ratio is at least $(\\bar\\Delta/(2N))^t$. By [P8] and $\\mu\\ge2$,\n\n$$\n\\frac{\\bar\\Delta}{2N}\n\\ge\n\\frac{\\mu(\\mu-1)}{2(p+1)^2}\n\\ge\\frac{\\epsilon^2}{4}.\n$$\n\nThis proves the simplified bound.\n\n### [P10] \u2014 proved: concurrency correction\n\nFix the seed set from [P9]. For a common neighbor $L$, partition the $t$ seed lines according to their intersection point with $L$. If fewer than $h$ distinct points occur, the partition creates at least $t-h+1$ colliding seed pairs. A fixed pair of seed lines can collide on at most the $p+1$ lines through their own intersection; a parallel pair contributes none. Double counting bad targets and colliding seed pairs gives\n\n$$\n|\\{L\\in N_H(S):h_L<h\\}|\n\\le\n\\frac{\\binom t2(p+1)}{t-h+1}.\n$$\n\nSubtracting this from the common-neighbor count proves Theorem 2. If an explainer vanishes identically on every seed graph, each of the $h_L$ distinct intersections is a distinct root on the target graph, so the correction measures the root supply relevant to interpolation.\n\n### [P11] \u2014 proved: direct DRC insertion is quantitatively insufficient\n\nIn the KTZ coefficient-count construction, interpolating $t$ seed graphs uses\n\n$$\nD_t=16(\\lfloor\\sqrt{dt}\\rfloor+1).\n$$\n\nEven before cleanup, transfer to a common-neighbor target needs $h_L>D_t$. Since $h_L\\le t$, this forces\n\n$$\nt>D_t>16\\sqrt{dt},\n\\qquad\\text{hence}\\qquad t>256d.\n$$\n\nReplacing the exact auxiliary moment $M_t(H)$ by the guarantee obtainable from acceptance density alone gives $N(\\epsilon^2/4)^t$. At the benchmark scale $\\epsilon=C(d/p)^{1/3}$, for fixed admissible $d$ and fixed $t>256d$,\n\n$$\nN(\\epsilon^2/4)^t\n=O_{C,d,t}(p^{2-2t/3})\n\\longrightarrow0.\n$$\n\nThus this black-box all-common-neighbor DRC certificate does not even guarantee one target line in the lower-boundary asymptotic regime. This does not rule out exploiting larger observed moments, label classes, or special structure in $H$.\n\n### [P12] \u2014 proved: scope of the obstruction\n\nThe carrier from [P3]--[P6] is connected, uses every line, attains all degree-distribution moment minima, and has essentially maximal universal reaching cost, yet $Q=0$ decodes it perfectly. Consequently, a valid stronger soundness proof may not treat moment regularity, broad support, connectivity, or large reaching cost alone as evidence of hardness. It must branch on polynomial-label or value coherence. This is a precise incidence-only obstruction, not a claim that every auxiliary or label-aware DRC argument fails.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output/status |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Degree means | $\\epsilon$ | none | $(p+1)\\epsilon$ and $p\\epsilon$; proved |\n| Repeated $s$-moment | $\\epsilon$ | $s$th power | at least $\\epsilon^s$; sharp; proved |\n| Distinct $s$-moment | mean degree | exact falling-factorial correction | $J_s(\\mu)/(n)_s$; sharp; proved |\n| Compatibility graph | $\\epsilon$ | two acceptances | density scale $\\epsilon^2$; proved |\n| Auxiliary DRC | compatibility density | $t$th power | density-only certificate $N(\\epsilon^2/4)^t$; proved under stated hypotheses |\n| Direct root supply | $D_t=16(\\lfloor\\sqrt{dt}\\rfloor+1)$ | $h\\le t$ | requires $t>256d$; proved |\n| Cubic-scale DRC substitution | $\\epsilon=C(d/p)^{1/3}$ | $\\epsilon^{2t}$ | $O(p^{2-2t/3})\\to0$ for fixed $t>256d$; proved |\n| Fractional reaching | $\\epsilon_0=d/p$ | one inverse $\\epsilon_0$ | $\\Theta(\\theta p/\\epsilon_0)$; proved |\n| KTZ selector | $\\epsilon$ | $\\epsilon^{-1}$ | $|R|=O(p/\\epsilon)$; quoted |\n| KTZ interpolation | $|R|$ | square root | $D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})$; reconstructed |\n| KTZ transfer | $D=O(\\epsilon p)$ | cubic comparison | $\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)$; reconstructed |\n| Constructed decoder | $f=0$ | none | global agreement $1$; proved |\n\nNo logarithmic, Markov, union, or Cauchy--Schwarz loss is hidden in the new results.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\nThe connected carrier is a successful counterexample to any universal claim that higher degree moments, connectivity, full support, or fractional relaxation automatically produce an $o(p/\\epsilon)$ reaching family. It is not a soundness counterexample: the labels visibly share $Q=0$.\n\nConcentrated good directions give a complementary stress test. Choose $k$ projective directions, put $f=0$, label their lines by zero and every other line by one. Every point has accepted degree $k$, so all point-centered with-replacement moments equal $\\epsilon^s$ exactly for $\\epsilon=k/(p+1)$. However, the auxiliary compatibility graph between two accepted parallel classes contains a $K_{p,p}$. Thus raw-graph $K_{2,2}$-freeness cannot be asserted for $H$.\n\nThe prior modal construction at ambient $d=101$ genuinely refutes a uniform exact-linear trigger $C d/p$ with global recovery $c\\epsilon$, but its local agreement is $\\Theta(\\log p/(p\\log\\log p))$, below every fixed $(101/p)^{1-\\eta}$ trigger. It does not obstruct the long-term target.\n\nA random point table with linewise interpolation guarantees roughly $d/p$ local agreement and can rule out exponents above one in suitable regimes. It does not yield a uniform fixed-$\\eta$ counterexample, especially when $d$ approaches $p$, and is not used in the theorem.\n\nNo inseparable construction affects the proof: $d<p$ prevents $t^p-t$ aliases. At $d=p-1$ the carrier remains valid and connected. At the lower boundary $d=101$, the first possible prime $p=103$ satisfies all denominators and root counts.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The field is exactly $\\mathbb F_p$ and $101\\le d<p$ throughout.\n- The set $S_d$ consists of distinct field elements. Each line label is a product of $d$ distinct linear factors and has exactly $d$ roots.\n- No derivative, Hasse derivative, discriminant, resultant, irreducibility, or absolute irreducibility input is used.\n- No field division by a derivative or slope occurs. Vertical lines are handled by their own parameterization.\n- The fractional division by $d-1$ is over the real weight space and is valid because $d\\ge101$.\n- The global polynomial $Q=0$ is a total-degree-at-most-$d$ decoder in an ambient test with $d>100$; no excluded degree parameter is analyzed.\n- The new proof has no Markov, union-bound, or Cauchy--Schwarz step. Discrete and ordinary Jensen losses are displayed exactly.\n- KTZ's Chernoff/union/Chebyshev selector losses belong only to the cited comparison and do not change its power of $\\epsilon$.\n- Finite computations were used only to check formulas, never to prove the asymptotic statements.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe benchmark is not improved, and no new global soundness theorem is claimed. The explicit carrier lies at $\\epsilon_0=d/p$, below every fixed $(d/p)^{1-\\eta}$ trigger because $0<d/p<1$, and it has a perfect decoder.\n\nThe $K_{2,2}$ obstruction applies only to the raw point-line incidence graph. Auxiliary compatibility graphs, factor graphs, and lifted incidence graphs may contain large bicliques. Theorem 2 is therefore a usable diagnostic rather than an impossibility theorem for all DRC variants.\n\nThe density-only lower bound for $M_t(H)$ can be far from the actual higher moment. A successful proof could exploit unusually large compatibility moments, provided it also controls concurrency and singular lifted roots. Conversely, the present note gives no realizable pseudorandom example proving that the auxiliary bound is sharp.\n\nFinally, moment and cover data discard polynomial labels.     def _static_check(self, role: str, response: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        note = response.get("note_markdown", "")
        errors: list[str] = []
        if len(note) < 1200:
            errors.append("academic note is shorter than 1200 characters")
        for heading in ("Abstract", "Theorem", "Exponent Ledger", "Limitations"):
            if heading.lower() not in note.lower():
                errors.append(f"missing {heading} section")
        if not response.get("proof_steps"):
            errors.append("no structured proof steps")
        if not response.get("exponent_ledger"):
            errors.append("no structured exponent ledger")
        if response.get("dimension") != 2:
            errors.append("submission dimension must be exactly 2")
        if response.get("field_regime") != "prime":
            errors.append("submission field_regime must be prime")
        if role == "researcher" and response.get("benchmark_improved"):
            if response.get("result_status") != "proved":
                errors.append("benchmark_improved requires result_status=proved")
            if not response.get("claimed_exponent"):
                errors.append("benchmark_improved requires a claimed exponent")
            elif response.get("claimed_exponent") not in {"1-o(1)", "1−o(1)"}:
                try:
                    if not is_stronger_fixed_exponent(
                            response["claimed_exponent"],
                            str(self.cfg.get("benchmark_exponent", "1/3"))):
                        errors.append("claimed exponent does not improve the configured benchmark")
                except (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError):
                    errors.append("claimed exponent is not a recognized rational or 1-o(1)")
        if role == "genius":
            snapshot = response.get("snapshot", {})
            if snapshot.get("coverage_complete") and snapshot.get("omitted_paths"):
                errors.append("coverage_complete conflicts with omitted_paths")
        return {
            "passed": not errors,
            "errors": errors,
            "note_sha256": hashlib.sha256(note.encode()).hexdigest(),
        }

    def _run_job(self, row: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, bool, str | None]:
        role, job_id = row["role"], row["id"]
        try:
            if role == "researcher":
                response, metadata = self.provider.run(
                    job_id, self._research_prompt(row), RESEARCH_SCHEMA)
                schema = "line-point-research-submission-v1"
            elif role == "genius":
                response, metadata = self.provider.run(
                    "GENIUS", self._genius_prompt(), GENIUS_SCHEMA)
                schema = "line-point-genius-synthesis-v1"
            else:
                source_id = str(row["dependency"])
                response, metadata = self.provider.run(
                    job_id, self._verifier_prompt(source_id), AUDIT_SCHEMA)
                schema = "line-point-proof-audit-v1"

            if role == "verifier":
                source_id = str(row["dependency"])
                source_response = json.loads(
                    (self.paths.campaign_dir / "submissions" / source_id / "response.json").read_text())
                claim = source_response.get("theorem_statement") or source_response.get(
                    "integrated_theorem", "")
                expected = hashlib.sha256(claim.encode()).hexdigest()
                accept_consistent = (
                    response["verified_claim_sha256"] == expected and
                    response["dimension_verified"] and
                    response["field_regime_verified"] and
                    response["coverage_complete"] and
                    not response["required_changes"] and
                    response["fatal_obstruction"] is None and
                    response["line_audit"] and
                    response["quantifier_audit"] and
                    response["exponent_audit"] and
                    all(item["verdict"] == "valid" for key in (
                        "line_audit", "quantifier_audit", "exponent_audit", "literature_audit")
                        for item in response[key])
                )
                if response["verdict"] == "accept" and not accept_consistent:
                    response["verdict"] = "revise"
                    response["unfixable"] = False
                    response["fatal_obstruction"] = None
                    response["required_changes"] = list(response["required_changes"]) + [
                        "Harness rejected an internally inconsistent accept verdict."]
                out_dir = self.paths.campaign_dir / "reviews" / source_id / job_id
                out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                (out_dir / "audit.json").write_text(
                    json.dumps(response, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
                (out_dir / "metadata.json").write_text(
                    json.dumps(metadata, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
            else:
                out_dir = self.paths.campaign_dir / "submissions" / job_id
                out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                static = self._static_check(role, response)
                (out_dir / "note.md").write_text(response["note_markdown"].rstrip() + "\n")
                (out_dir / "response.json").write_text(
                    json.dumps(response, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
                (out_dir / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps({
                    "schema": schema,
            model=str(self.cfg.get("model", "gpt-5.6-sol")),
            reasoning_effort=str(self.cfg.get("reasoning_effort", "ultra")),
            disable_nested_agents=True,
            timeout_seconds=int(self.cfg.get("roadmap_timeout_seconds", 5400)),
        )

    def corpus_snapshot(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        patterns = (
            "submissions/*/response.json",
            "reviews/*/*/audit.json",
            "lemma_book/submissions/*/response.json",
        )
        paths = sorted({
            path for pattern in patterns
            for path in self.paths.campaign_dir.glob(pattern)
            if path.is_file()
        })
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        receipts = []
        for path in paths:
            relative = path.relative_to(self.paths.workspace).as_posix()
            value = file_sha256(path)
            digest.update(relative.encode())
            digest.update(value.encode())
            receipts.append({"path": relative, "sha256": value})
        evidence: dict[str, Any] = {}
        submissions_root = self.paths.campaign_dir / "submissions"
        for response_path in sorted(submissions_root.glob("*/response.json")):
            source_job_id = response_path.parent.name
            source = json.loads(response_path.read_text())
            source_sha = hashlib.sha256(
                json.dumps(source, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
            claim = source.get("theorem_statement") or source.get("integrated_theorem", "")
            claim_sha = hashlib.sha256(str(claim).encode()).hexdigest()
            audit_path = (self.paths.campaign_dir / "reviews" / source_job_id /
                          f"verifier-{source_job_id}" / "audit.json")
            audit = json.loads(audit_path.read_text()) if audit_path.exists() else None
            audit_exact = bool(
                audit and audit.get("verified_claim_sha256") == claim_sha)
            lemma_path = self.paths.campaign_dir / "lemma_book" / "submissions" / source_job_id / "response.json"
            lemma_parts: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
            if lemma_path.exists():
                lemma_response = json.loads(lemma_path.read_text())
                for lemma in lemma_response.get("lemmas", []):
                    lemma_parts.setdefault(str(lemma.get("source_step_id", "")), []).append(
                        str(lemma.get("id", "")))
            for step in source.get("proof_steps", []):
                key = "|".join((source_job_id, str(step["id"]), source_sha))
                evidence[key] = {
                    "source_job_id": source_job_id,
                    "source_step_id": str(step["id"]),
                    "source_response_sha256": source_sha,
                    "source_status": step.get("status", "conditional"),
                    "audit_verdict": audit.get("verdict") if audit else "pending",
                    "audit_exact": audit_exact,
                    "lemma_ids": sorted(lemma_parts.get(str(step["id"]), [])),
                }
        payload = {"sha256": digest.hexdigest(), "files": receipts, "evidence": evidence}
        (self.root / "corpus-index.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
        return payload
